records.outputs: Epistemic event graphs; scores on four competence axes (evidence, experiment, revision, no reward hacking); six descriptive persona traits
records.notes: ARA Lab with authors from Michigan, MIT, Ohio State and UC Davis. Scores how an agent forms, tests and revises claims from its execution record alone, without reference answers or outcome scores. LLM judges extract acts and claims with exact quotes, which code checks against the record, and answer closed questions by majority vote; code does all counting. Has no task set of its own: the paper scores 119 existing runs from PostTrainBench, Chip-Bench and the nanoGPT speedrun (ML and hardware engineering tasks). Judge outputs and call logs are released. MIT code; the paper's scored runs are on Hugging Face under CC BY 4.0. Measures research process quality, not the correctness of final results.

records.name: OSWorld-Science
records.domain: Computer-use agents operating professional scientific software

repo_links.label: Hugging Face (gated data and VM images)

records.inputs: 146 expert-defined tasks across seven domains and 17 scientific software tools, run in KVM virtual machines through screenshot-based GUI and optional command-line actions
records.outputs: Partial-credit scores from task-specific evaluators that inspect generated artifacts and application state, plus trajectories and cost reports
records.notes: Multi-institution benchmark (Tsinghua, Yale and others) covering chemistry, physics, medicine, statistics, biology, GIS and linguistics workflows in tools such as QuPath, ASKCOS, OpenFOAM and PyMOL. The paper treats ScienceBoard as related work; the two are separate benchmarks. The repository is CC BY 4.0, while task data, grader references and VM images are CC BY-NC 4.0 behind manual Hugging Face approval; third-party software keeps its own terms. Public images contain no licensed software: SAS and Mnova steps need the user's own licences, and the 14 Ansys Fluent tasks need a self-built Windows guest and an Ansys licence. Requires Linux x86-64 with KVM and Docker. The published data include answer keys.

access_evidence.software_license: CC-BY-4.0 repository (not a software licence); task data, graders and VM images CC-BY-NC-4.0 behind manual approval; third-party and licensed software under own terms

records.name: BIABench
records.domain: End-to-end bioimage analysis reconstructed from published studies
records.inputs: 16 tasks with raw 2D, 3D and time-lapse images and basic or expert instructions
records.outputs: Outcome scores against study ground truth plus VLM-judged process scores
records.notes: Benchmark of 16 tasks from H&E histology to single-molecule localization microscopy, with adapters for Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness, Biomni and two Fiji-based agents (CopilotJ, Agentic-J; the authors co-developed Agentic-J). The harness is BSD-3-Clause. Task data on Hugging Face (11.1 GB zipped) keep per-task source licences (CC BY 4.0 or 3.0, CC BY-SA 4.0, CC0, GPL-3.0, and EMBL-EBI Terms of Use for one task), and the authors' own specs, rubrics and derived ground truth are CC BY 4.0. Part of the work used ELIXIR Estonia infrastructure at the University of Tartu.

records.name: MolDesignBench
records.domain: Scenario-grounded molecular generation and optimization with chemistry tools
records.inputs: 2,000 design narratives (1,800 feasible, 200 infeasible) with implied and explicit property and functional-group constraints
records.outputs: Proposed molecules or infeasibility judgements, scored with and without 17 chemistry tools (success, constraint satisfaction, infeasibility accuracy, validity, tool calls)
records.notes: Korea University and LG AI Research benchmark (COLM 2026) for tool-augmented LLM agents, capped at 20 interaction turns per instance. The best evaluated agent reaches about 43% success. Two property-range design tools require an NVIDIA MolMIM NIM with NGC credentials. Code is MIT; the benchmark questions on Hugging Face are CC BY-NC 4.0 and, per the dataset card, also subject to the Terms of Use of the model used to create them (Claude Opus 4.6). Computational scoring only; no synthesis or wet-lab validation.

access_evidence.software_license: MIT code; CC-BY-NC-4.0 benchmark questions, which the dataset card also makes subject to the Terms of Use of the generating model (Anthropic Opus 4.6)

records.name: MechBench
records.domain: Mechanism discovery beyond phenomenological laws from observational data
records.inputs: Observational training data and scientific context for each task; hidden mechanistic models, including mutated variants of canonical mechanisms, generate the data
records.outputs: Observable-law accuracy on train, in-distribution and out-of-distribution data, plus mechanism-probe scores
records.notes: Benchmark from a Tsinghua University-led team (repository in the tsinghua-fib-lab GitHub organization). It scores two things separately: recovery of an observable law and recovery of the hidden mechanism behind it. The Full-set has 512 synthetic instances from 16 task families in physics, chemistry, biology and materials science, built as mutated variants of canonical mechanisms. The paper evaluates Codex, Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness configurations. Scoring uses symbolic equivalence and numerical accuracy with no LLM judge. The repository is MIT-licensed, forked from yuzhTHU/mdbench. It bundles the task library, task-validation, export and scoring code, and baseline run results. Not the same system as MECHBench (arXiv 2511.10821), a black-box optimization benchmark from structural mechanics.

records.name: RECLAIM
records.domain: Reproducing central empirical claims of machine-learning papers
records.inputs: 100 NeurIPS 2025 papers (plus a 14-paper development split), each with whatever its authors released, a fixed target value with tolerance, and a GPU budget of up to 96 H100-hours; Run, Retrain and Reimplement tiers
records.outputs: Per-run 0-10 audit score and verdict (reproduced, partial, not reproduced, unverifiable, disqualified) assigned by an LLM auditor from logs and outputs; per-tier reproduction rates
records.notes: Salunkhe, Ding, Verma, Kindratenko (UIUC/NCSA). Tiers follow what the authors released: code, data and weights (Run), no weights (Retrain), no code (Reimplement). Claude Sonnet 5 grades each run from execution evidence, not the agent's own report (F1 0.82 against human graders). Of four agents tested, the best per tier reproduced 41% (Run), 27% (Retrain) and 15% (Reimplement). Designed to be rebuilt yearly from new conferences. MIT code; splits and 372 run records under CC BY 4.0, also on Hugging Face; the repository still describes itself as an anonymized release under review.

records.name: TraceML
records.domain: Development-process comparison of ML-engineering auto-research agents with human Kaggle practice
records.inputs: A finished ML-engineering agent run (git sidecar with scored tags, AIDE/MLEvolve search journal, or git workspace tracking submission.csv); for recording new runs, any command-line agent plus MLE-bench-prepared competition data
records.outputs: Version-level trajectory with state and action labels in the dataset schema, and a behaviour report comparing the run with 4,465 human Kaggle trajectories and the paper's Codex and MLEvolve runs
records.notes: Carnegie Mellon dataset and toolkit that records ML development as scored, labelled code versions. On seven Kaggle competitions it pairs 430 human trajectories with 207 agent trajectories from 31 Codex CLI and MLEvolve runs (MLEvolve searches split into branches), showing agents stuck in narrow edit loops. Apache-2.0 toolkit and labeler models; dataset mostly CC BY 4.0 (GPT-5-mini labels may not train competing LLMs). Labelling needs a CUDA GPU. ML engineering only. Not the Polyaxon or TraceOpt 'traceml' tools.

records.name: SA-Bench (SemanticAlign-Bench)
records.domain: Semantic fidelity of agent-generated ML paper-reproduction code
records.inputs: Paper specification plus an agent-generated reproduction repository for each of 30 ICLR, ICML and NeurIPS 2025 ML papers
records.outputs: Five-level per-claim scores over 1,491 human-verified Semantic Alignment Units, aggregated into numerical, method, protocol and ordering drift diagnostics
records.notes: Benchmark by authors at Beihang University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Minzu University of China and Peking University (corresponding author at Peking University). Accepted to Findings of EMNLP 2026 according to the arXiv comment. It measures semantic drift, where reproduction code runs but departs from the paper's specification. Scoring is static: dimension-specific LLM judges compare code text against atomic implementation claims, and the generated code is never executed. A deterministic mode without an LLM judge is also available. ML papers only. Ships BasicAgent, PaperCoder and OpenHands baseline runs. MIT code; CC BY 4.0 annotations on Hugging Face.

records.name: DeltaML-Bench
records.domain: Improving published baselines inside real machine-learning research repositories
records.inputs: 48 tasks sourced from Papers With Code, each with the paper PDF, original code repository, dataset and published baseline metric, run under time and token budgets
records.outputs: Percentage improvement over the published baseline, per-run success rates and integrity checks for specification gaming
records.notes: Algorithmic Research Group benchmark run on METR's Vivaria platform. The paper compares GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4 under a modular scaffold and ARG's search-based scaffold, and reports specification-gaming rates up to 47.9% in modular runs. The public repo ships task families, anti-cheat checks, graders and modular agents; the ARG agent folder named in its README was removed in March 2026. Root licence Apache-2.0; the bundled Vivaria and task folders carry METR MIT licences. Most tasks need a GPU, Docker and model API keys.

records.name: ExplorationBench
records.domain: Hypothesis-driven exploration of executable rule worlds that conflict with prior knowledge
records.inputs: A flawed manual, fixed worked examples and a single probing tool with deterministic feedback, over four exploration rounds per sandbox (AlienCode, AlienLogic)
records.outputs: Rule reports and held-out task answers from tool-disabled copies at each milestone, checked exactly by an interpreter or proof checker (no LLM judge)
records.notes: Benchmark from Fudan University, Tencent Hunyuan and Tsinghua University that measures whether AI systems acquire unfamiliar rules by probing an alien calculation language (AlienCode) and a patched natural-deduction logic (AlienLogic): 55 discovery targets, 140 held-out tasks, ten frontier systems evaluated. Apache-2.0 code releases the harness, scoring, evaluation engines and two small demo worlds; the evaluation worlds stay private, so leaderboard scores require a maintainer-run evaluation and demo scores are not comparable. The worlds contain no science-domain content, and the authors state the benchmark does not measure real scientific discovery.

records.name: AgentIdeaBench
records.domain: Scientific ideation under static versus agentic literature access
records.inputs: Subfield name plus a Semantic Scholar search/fetch tool with a 10-call budget (Active) or the subfield plus 5 fixed reference papers (Static); 100 subfields in five disciplines, 40 densely scored
records.outputs: One-paragraph hypotheses scored 1-10 by three LLM critics against retrieved prior art on originality, feasibility, clarity, impact and specificity; Static-vs-Active leaderboard and released scores and search traces
records.notes: HKUST KnowComp benchmark (with NVIDIA co-authors) reporting matched static and active evaluations of 33 LLMs. Active retrieval separates models more than static reference sets do. Scores are LLM-critic judgments; the authors note that originality is the least validated dimension. Code is MIT and released data are CC BY 4.0. Measures idea generation; hypotheses are not tested experimentally. Distinct from IdeaBench (asa-ideabench).

records.name: SciExam for ENSO
aliases: AI Science Exam for El Nino-Southern Oscillation
records.domain: Building low-order stochastic ENSO climate models from observations
records.inputs: Raw ocean-atmosphere observations for 1980-2014, background material and a reference paper; a six-hour budget split into data processing, diagnostic writing and model building
records.outputs: Agent-built stochastic ENSO models scored by hidden graders on ENSO statistics, recovery of unobserved variables and forecasts of held-out years (2015-2024); released runs and checkpoints
records.notes: Benchmark by authors from Ohio State, Yale, UC San Diego, Stanford and Princeton. Agents process observations into indices, write their own diagnostics, which are then frozen, and use only those as feedback while building the model. Hidden numerical graders, with no LLM reviewer, score each model and a published reference model the same way; twelve agent systems are evaluated. The sciexam code and the agent-written model files are MIT; the other released records are CC BY 4.0, with third-party data terms listed. Sandboxed grading uses Docker, and rerunning agents needs the user's own provider accounts. Computational modelling only.

records.name: WhatWorkedBench
records.domain: Inferring experimental effects of workflow changes under measurement budgets
records.inputs: Executable workflow code, two free anchor measurements (all-zero and all-one configurations) and a budget of purchasable measurements, across 36 task conditions
records.outputs: Predicted response surfaces scored on component effects, interactions, configuration choice and delivery
records.notes: Carnegie Mellon and Tsinghua benchmark of how much research agents learn from a limited number of experiments; references come from exhaustive native CPU execution. Apache-2.0 release with the task catalog, budgeted evaluator, numerical baselines and replay evidence; third-party datasets keep their upstream terms, some limited to scientific use. Workflows are ML tasks such as classification, forecasting and image restoration; the paper evaluates DeepSeek V4 Flash and Pro agents.

records.name: Ascent
records.domain: Pharmacoepidemiological analysis of real-world clinical data
records.inputs: Natural-language epidemiological questions and cohort eligibility criteria over OMOP-CDM or native-schema clinical warehouses, through a shared Model Context Protocol tool server
records.outputs: Medical code lists, SQL, patient cohorts with attrition funnels and baseline summaries, and answers with inspectable intermediate results
records.notes: Bayer AG system used internally for expert-supervised analysis of real-world clinical data. An LLM orchestrator plans, calls medical-coding, question-answering, cohort and SQL tools on a shared Model Context Protocol server that any MCP client can drive, inspects intermediate results and re-plans; underspecified questions go back to the user to confirm an interpretation. The public BSD-3-Clause distribution is a demonstration on generated patients and synthetic vocabularies, ships the EpiTrap set of designed-in pharmacoepidemiological errors, and needs an external LLM API key. Reported gains over a fixed pipeline came with more tool calls and longer runtimes; evaluation used one Optum EHR source with LLM grading, and the system does not estimate causal effects.

records.name: LabAgent
records.domain: Reproducing and extending a laboratory's computational life-science methods
records.inputs: A laboratory's code repositories or papers, a reproduction target or analysis task, staged datasets and a run budget
records.outputs: Execution-validated skill packages, reproduced metrics and figures with scripts and logs, benchmark answers, and a memory of failure fixes
records.notes: Yale-led harness, with Northeastern, Broad Institute and Stanford co-authors. Its explore stage turns a repository or paper into a skill that enters the library only after it installs and runs end to end; its reproduce stage executes the skill on mini-swe-agent and reads back commands that fixed failures in earlier runs. Evaluated on drug-property prediction (TDC ADMET), biomedical data analysis (BiomniBench-DA, GeneBench-Pro), protein variant-effect prediction (ProteinGym) and statistical-genetics fine-mapping, where it partly rebuilt a figure from the authors' own laboratory: two of the five methods were agent-written surrogates and one ran with a misread flag. Comparisons with Claude Code and Codex use one run per target. MIT code ships the 63 skills used in the manuscript; the repository states that BiomniBench tasks were scored by keyword overlap instead of that benchmark's LLM judge. Setup uses an Anthropic API key. Computational only, no laboratory execution.

records.name: T-REX (agentic binder design)
records.domain: De novo protein binder design campaign control
records.inputs: A design target, available GPUs, a campaign duration and an output directory
records.outputs: Structurally distinct in-silico binder hits with campaign archives for analysis
records.notes: Princeton (Zhong lab) framework in which planner and supervisor LLMs, run as a locally served Qwen model via vLLM, decide whether to rescue, explore or exploit while a deterministic controller validates and schedules generation, redesign and evaluation jobs across Proteina-Complexa, BindCraft and BoltzGen. Across seven targets it allocated compute in a target-dependent way and yielded more structurally distinct in-silico hits than the baselines evaluated (PUCT, epsilon-greedy, generator-only and SMAC3); the paper states it was assessed only computationally and that experimental validation of its designs remains to be done. The T-REX code is MIT, with a verified installation profile targeting Linux and H100 GPUs under Slurm; the orchestrated backends and model assets keep their upstream licences, PyRosetta included.

records.name: MOMbot
records.domain: Robotic multimodal interventions on Xenopus embryos, organoids and cells; closed loop demonstrated on organoids
records.inputs: Operator-loaded biological material, a human-specified objective and a stimulus search space (in the closed-loop demonstration, electrical-stimulation duration from 1 to 300 s)
records.outputs: Interventions chosen by the active learner and executed on the robot, image-derived organoid velocity measurements and an updated duration-response model
records.notes: Robot scientist from the University of Vermont, Tufts University and Harvard (Wyss Institute, Harvard Medical School) with five two-dish stations, four stimulus modalities (chemical, electrical, mechanical, thermal) and high-resolution imaging; the hardware was validated on Xenopus embryos, mucociliary organoids and dissociated ectodermal cells. In the closed-loop demonstration an upper-confidence-bound active learner chose electrical-stimulation durations and the robot applied them to 55 motile mucociliary organoids over eight rounds (about 12 hours across two days), updating the model after each round from a warm start of 29 random interventions. A human operator loads biological material and assigns each dish to AI or human control. No language model is involved. The MIT-licensed repository holds the AI/control software and figure-reproduction data; the custom hardware is described only in the paper.

records.name: MicroClaw
records.domain: Natural-language microscope control and adaptive image acquisition
records.inputs: Natural-language acquisition requests, a Micro-Manager-controlled microscope, a user-reviewed safety configuration and the user's own Anthropic API key
records.outputs: Executed imaging workflows, compiled Pycro-Manager scripts and inspectable session histories
records.notes: Microscopy agent from Max Perutz Labs, University of Vienna, and collaborators. It drives Micro-Manager microscopes through Pycro-Manager using Claude models via the Anthropic API. The authors call it pseudo-agentic, and most use is collaborative workflow development. On real instruments it also scanned coverslips with agent-written analysis hooks, switched channels and acquired time-lapses without user input. Disclosed gates: a user-defined safety configuration is enforced before every hardware call; enabling illumination and above-threshold acquisitions require user confirmation, which can be granted per session; agent-written hooks need explicit user approval before they run. The repository says the safety features are not comprehensive and the BSD-3-Clause release is a preview not suited to production. Acquired data and session history files are on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0. It is unrelated to the identically named OpenClaw-family chat assistants on GitHub, such as microclaw/microclaw.

records.name: LabscriptAI
records.domain: Liquid-handling robot scripting and gated execution for synthetic biology
records.inputs: Natural-language experimental intent or community protocols, human-confirmed standard operating procedures, and robot hardware and deck constraints
records.outputs: Simulator-validated platform-specific robot scripts (Opentrons Python, PyLabRobot, Tecan .gwl), gated runtime recovery actions on Opentrons robots, execution traces, and repository-formatted records (protocols.io, FPbase)
records.notes: Execution-aware agent harness from the Shenzhen Institute of Synthetic Biology (Chinese Academy of Sciences) with Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory co-authors. An authoring loop turns a human-confirmed SOP into a platform-specific liquid-handling script and repairs it against simulator feedback (Opentrons Flex and OT-2, Hamilton via PyLabRobot, Tecan Fluent .gwl worklists). A runtime loop reads Opentrons controller state after a failed command and proposes a bounded recovery, which a deterministic gatekeeper allows, holds for more evidence or human confirmation, or suspends; live recovery was tested on an Opentrons Flex only (six matched fault pairs). Reported deployments include cell-free characterisation of 854 GFP designs from 171 student teams in the CAPE 2025-2026 challenges, containment-aware engineering of a formaldehyde-converting enzyme, and robot scripts for assembling 531 genetic parts into the 2025 iGEM Distribution Kit, with manual purification and inter-station transfers where needed. Experimental goals stay human-defined; the authors state that adaptation based on biological outcomes was not tested, and the README leaves sequence screening in deployment to the operator. The README and package metadata declare MIT, but the repository has no LICENSE file and the v3 preprint says code will be provided in a subsequent version, so access is source-available; the Zenodo deposit holds CC BY 4.0 study data without source code.

access_evidence.software_license: MIT declared in the README ('License: MIT') and in labscriptai/pyproject.toml; no LICENSE file in the repository tree and the GitHub licence endpoint returns 404 (checked 2026-10-10); the v3 preprint's code-availability statement says the code will be provided in a subsequent version

records.name: iCloudBiofoundry
records.domain: Cloud-accessible agentic design with robotic execution for synthetic biology
records.inputs: Natural-language research objectives entered in the platform's web interface, optionally with prior experimental data or uploaded literature
records.outputs: Designs, hypotheses and wet-lab protocols; simulation-checked robotic workflows that run at connected biofoundries after administrator approval; measured results returned to the user for the next design round
records.notes: Cloud platform from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (Huimin Zhao laboratory). The iBioGenie multi-agent layer plans work from literature, databases and computational tools; BiofoundryAI compiles its protocols into simulation-checked workflows for the iBioFAB and iBioFoundry robotic facilities. Case studies: phytase re-engineering seeded with data from an earlier campaign, PAND enzyme discovery followed by a second engineering round on the best hit, and CRISPR knockout engineering of yeast beta-carotene production. Human gates: researchers approve plans, administrators approve every instrument job, an operator sets up and starts each run, and the authors chose the second-round PAND target and manually finalised the 32 discovery candidates. Portal access needs federated sign-in and an administrator-approved request. Source code is promised on acceptance; the four GitHub repositories the portal lists returned 404 on 2026-10-10, and the Momentum scheduler is a commercial Thermo Fisher product.

records.name: Andromeda 2 (Intrepid Labs)
records.domain: Agentic pharmaceutical formulation design in an automated laboratory
records.inputs: Target product profile, permitted excipient composition grid with hard constraints, structured in-house formulation evidence, automated formulation laboratory
records.outputs: 16-formulation SEDDS batches with rationales, prepared by liquid-handling robots and assayed automatically (biorelevant dissolution with HPLC, dynamic light scattering), followed by successor batches informed by the measurements
records.notes: Language-model agentic system from Intrepid Labs (Toronto), the successor to the company's non-agentic probabilistic optimiser Andromeda 1. Proposal, critique, review and planning steps call the Andromeda 1 models and other tools; a deterministic feasibility engine checks each batch before robotic preparation and automated assays. In one six-batch (96-formulation) paclitaxel campaign per arm, 50% of its formulations reached the pooled upper-quartile AUC threshold, against 17% for Andromeda 1 and 2% for a wet-lab DoE; 12, 6 and 0 met all four target-product criteria. Endpoints are in-vitro dissolution, and the authors note single campaigns limit inference. A formulation scientist reviewed every batch before execution without changing it, and all arms shared the same operators. The paper describes no code, model or data release.

records.name: cryoAgent
records.domain: Autonomous single-particle cryo-EM image processing
records.inputs: Cryo-EM movies (or pre-corrected micrographs) with microscope and acquisition parameters, approximate particle diameter, expected symmetry and CryoSPARC project settings
records.outputs: Three-dimensional reconstructions with quality metrics, heterogeneity (structural-state) analyses, processing-state histories, LLM logs and end-of-run reports
records.notes: Agent from Fei Sun's group (Guangzhou Institutes of Biomedicine and Health and Institute of Biophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences) that runs a reason-act-observe loop over CryoSPARC jobs with three autonomy levels: a rigid baseline workflow, guided optimisation and heterogeneity analysis, then hypothesis-driven exploration of alternative processing strategies. It also searches the CryoSPARC forum to recover from job failures. The authors report better reconstructions than the automated workflow cryoWizard on the datasets compared, and a previously unreported isolated 60S ribosome population in EMPIAR-10028 found by the heterogeneity agent. Processing is computational only, on existing EMPIAR data; the microscope is not controlled. Apache-2.0 code; a licensed CryoSPARC installation (tested up to 4.7.1) and an external LLM API are required, and the RELION interface is experimental. Distinct from unlicensed GitHub projects named CryoAgent by other developers.

records.name: PRAXIS (protein engineering)
records.domain: Autonomous protein engineering in a robotic laboratory
records.inputs: Parent enzyme sequences, a defined combinatorial sequence space and substrate-specificity objectives
records.outputs: Designed variants built and characterised by the robotic laboratory, with an updated sequence-function model
records.notes: Platform from Philip Romero's laboratory at Duke University, with a co-author at Harvard Medical School, that couples a ProteinNPT-based generative protein language model to an automated laboratory doing gene assembly, cell-free expression and fluorescence enzyme assays. Three agents sharing one learning model ran 25 rounds over about one month without human intervention and shifted Family 1 glycoside hydrolase specificity toward non-native sugars; 132 variants were characterised, and top variants were later re-assayed by hand for verification. Humans stocked the laboratory with all DNA fragments and reagents before the campaign began. It builds on the same group's earlier SAMPLE self-driving laboratory. Apache-2.0 code covers the agent, the in-silico deep-mutational-scanning benchmarks and the laboratory-environment software; the agent and benchmarks run with no laboratory hardware, while wet execution needs the physical platform. The preprint text itself is CC BY-NC.

records.name: Autonomous enzyme engineering platform (iBioFAB)
aliases: A generalized platform for artificial intelligence-powered autonomous enzyme engineering
records.domain: Autonomous enzyme engineering on a biofoundry
records.inputs: A protein sequence and a quantifiable fitness assay, with a natural-language (LLM) interface for campaign setup
records.outputs: Robot-built and assayed variant libraries, fitness measurements and an improved enzyme variant per round
records.notes: Platform from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (Zhao laboratory) combining an ESM-2 protein language model, the EVmutation epistasis model and a low-N supervised model with the iBioFAB biofoundry, which automates mutagenesis PCR, DNA assembly, transformation, colony picking, plasmid purification, expression and enzyme assays. Four rounds over four weeks screened 446 AtHMT and 448 YmPhytase variants, giving a 16-fold improvement in halide methyltransferase ethyltransferase activity (and a ~90-fold shift in substrate preference) plus a 26-fold improvement for the phytase at neutral pH. The authors self-assess the degree of automation as between level 3 (conditional automation) and level 4, with steps inside each module needing little if any human intervention. Released code covers the prediction models (MIT) and primer and worklist generation (BSD-3-Clause), archived on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.15233300, 10.5281/zenodo.15243671; both deposits declare MIT); the robotic workflows need the institutional facility and a commercial scheduler, and the authors list model and mutagenesis limitations. Distinct from PLMeAE, SAMPLE and the 2026 AI-native autonomous biofoundry.

records.name: Agentomics
records.domain: Autonomous machine-learning model development for biomedical data
records.inputs: A folder-based dataset split for a classification or regression task, with an optional data description and supplementary material; user-set run time, LLM backbone and validation metric
records.outputs: The best iteration's trained model with training and inference scripts and a conda environment, plus a PDF report of the approach and its train, validation and (if a test set is given) test metrics
records.notes: Agent from the Centre for Molecular Medicine and Biobanking, University of Malta, that runs iterative ML experiments inside a Docker container: an experiment-design model plans each iteration from earlier iteration summaries, and seven validated steps, from data exploration to prediction exploration, yield one working model per iteration. It can draw on pre-downloaded biomedical foundation models such as ESM-2, Nucleotide Transformer and ChemBERTa. In the Bioinformatics (ISMB 2026) evaluation on 20 protein-engineering, drug-discovery and regulatory-genomics datasets, it beat the other agent systems tested and produced new state-of-the-art models on 11 of 20 benchmarks. MIT licensed and pip-installable; runs with hosted LLM APIs or local Ollama models. Its outputs are predictive models, not biological hypotheses or experiments. Not the same as OpenMS/agentomics, a collection of pyopenms tools.

records.name: scBench
records.domain: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis by AI agents
records.inputs: AnnData snapshots captured immediately before an analysis step, with natural-language task prompts
records.outputs: Structured JSON answers scored pass/fail by deterministic graders on recovery of a key biological result, with per-model, per-task and per-platform accuracy, cost and agent trajectories
records.notes: LatchBio benchmark of single-cell RNA-seq analysis problems across six sequencing platforms and task categories from quality control to differential expression, run by agents in code-executing harnesses (the paper uses mini-SWE-agent capped at 100 steps). The arXiv v1 paper reports 394 problems in seven categories with 30 public examples; the current repository describes a revised set of 195 problems in six categories, of which six are public and the rest withheld to limit training contamination. The scbench repository (CLI, evaluation specs, results, trajectories) is Apache-2.0, but the graders and agent harness it depends on come from LatchBio's latch-eval-tools, whose licence file reserves all rights, and evaluation data are fetched from Latch Data through the Latch SDK. Earlier companion to the catalogued scBench-Long, which cites it and shares authors. Unrelated to the SCBench benchmarks for KV-cache methods and sports commentary.

access_evidence.software_license: Mixed: scbench wrapper Apache-2.0; required graders/harness dependency latch-eval-tools is '© LatchBio LLC. All rights reserved.' (checked 2026-10-10); 189 of 195 evaluations withheld

records.name: SpatialBench (spatial biology agents)
records.domain: Spatial transcriptomics analysis by AI agents
records.inputs: Spatial-omics analysis states snapshotted immediately before a target step, with task prompts
records.outputs: Structured answers scored pass/fail by deterministic graders (numeric tolerance, multiple choice, marker-gene precision/recall, label-set Jaccard, distribution comparison) against a key biological result
records.notes: LatchBio benchmark covering five spatial transcriptomics platforms and seven task categories; the arXiv version reports 146 problems and the revised repository 159. Only 16 example evaluations, aggregate results and agent trajectories are public under Apache-2.0, and the full set is withheld to limit contamination. Task data load from latch:// nodes on the Latch platform. The graders and runner come from the required latch-eval-tools package, whose licence reads 'All rights reserved' and whose repository is archived. The paper reports large harness effects, with the authors' own Latch harness scoring highest for Opus-4.5 (61.7% vs 48.1% under Claude Code). Unrelated to other arXiv benchmarks named SpatialBench (spatial foundation models; multimodal spatial cognition) and SpatialBench-UC (text-to-image).

records.name: MetaClaw (metagenomics, HUST/BGI)
records.domain: Metagenomic and microbiome multi-omics analysis with provenance
records.inputs: A natural-language analysis request with a FlowHub path to raw shotgun reads, or pre-computed abundance and metabolite tables, plus sample metadata
records.outputs: Statistical results, figures and an HTML report, plus a per-job reproducibility bundle of parameters, generated scripts, container definitions, cloud submission specs and logs
records.notes: Metagenomics and microbiome multi-omics agent from Huazhong University of Science and Technology and BGI Genomics, built on the OpenClaw gateway. Quality control, host-read removal, profiling and assembly run as versioned flows on the FlowHub cloud platform; statistics, machine learning, figures and reports run in network-isolated containers from reference scripts the language model adapts to each cohort. The user confirms input bindings before any cloud job is submitted. On the full cohorts of four published studies (769 metagenomic profiles) it recovered 4/4, 3/3, 4/5 and 5/5 of the reported marker sets; downstream validity varied with the model backend and prompt detail. MIT licensed; end-to-end runs need a FlowHub account, and the July 2026 repository lacks the guides its README links to and benchmark files for one of the four studies. Independent of aiming-lab's MetaClaw (arXiv 2603.17187), a general self-improving OpenClaw agent.

records.name: PerturbTrace
records.domain: Feedback use by closed-loop perturbation-discovery agents
records.inputs: 17 screen-derived perturbation tasks (target, candidate identifiers, round budget) with hidden-oracle feedback under true, random or no-feedback conditions, run through a Codex-based launcher or a harness CLI with an externally supplied solver skill
records.outputs: Final hit recall and machine-readable run traces, plus stage-wise Feedback-to-State, State-to-Action and Action-to-Outcome diagnostics for each round-to-round transition
records.notes: Benchmark from DeepAutonomy Technology (Beijing) with 17 tasks derived from public perturbation resources: CRISPR knockout and activation screens (primary T cells, CAR-T, NK cells, phagocytosis, tau, choline recycling), DepMap/Achilles and Project DRIVE RNAi dependencies, GDSC2 drug response and JUMP Cell Painting morphology; some tasks are imported from the BioDiscoveryAgent task suite. It tests whether feedback appears in an agent's stated rationale, whether that rationale guides the next perturbation batch and whether the batch beats random sampling. The preprint runs BioDiscoveryAgent, Biomni, Codex and Codex with a restricted strategy on a GPT-5.5 backend against random, active-learning and LLM-guided Bayesian-optimisation baselines; 43 of 576 feedback-bearing transitions completed the full sequence, 25 of them under random feedback. The MIT repository ships task manifests, normalised oracle scores and hit sets, the harness and the trace evaluator, with a Codex-only runtime adapter; the non-agent baselines were not found in it, and the README describes a research release with fuller packaging planned. Distinct from PerTurboAgent.

records.name: PhenoAIR
records.domain: Mechanism-of-action inference from Cell Painting morphological profiles
records.inputs: Query compound Cell Painting profile and chemical structure (SMILES), plus a reference panel of profiled compounds with mechanism annotations
records.outputs: Predicted mechanism of action (or 'novel' in the open-set mode) with alternative candidates, a confidence level, written reasoning, and the full agent/controller trajectory, candidate memory and tool log
records.notes: Multi-agent framework that treats retrieved morphological neighbours as uncertain evidence to be weighed and sometimes rejected. A phenotype agent and a structure-side mechanism agent update a shared candidate memory; a rule-based controller picks further evidence views until it stops; an LLM arbiter then decides, followed by deterministic eligibility checks. Offline reference-set calibration scores source reliability, phenotype stability and mechanism confusion. Evaluated on a JUMP Cell Painting benchmark in controlled, realistic and open-world settings. MIT code; the Hugging Face dataset declares no licence. The repository states the default runtime does not yet reproduce the paper pipeline (uncalibrated retrieval, external mechanism-data adapters not yet included).

records.name: Enrich.AI
records.domain: Gene-set enrichment analysis and biological interpretation
records.inputs: A gene list with a short description of the biological context, in a conversational interface
records.outputs: Enrichment statistics, literature-grounded written interpretation and interactive visualisations
records.notes: Agent from the Ionian University (Corfu) that runs a reason-act-observe loop over five tools: enrichment against Enrichr gene-set libraries, Enrichr library queries, MyGene.info gene annotation, Europe PMC literature search, and text-mined paper annotations. It then writes an interpretation with six visualisation types. Uses Gemini 2.5 Flash by default; the code also accepts OpenAI-compatible APIs. The preprint's reliability evaluation on 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets used an LLM judge. MIT licensed, with tagged releases and a hosted Streamlit app; the chat interface is explicitly human-in-the-loop.

records.name: LungChat
records.domain: Conversational multi-omics analysis and drug repurposing in lung biology
records.inputs: Natural-language questions over curated single-cell and spatial lung datasets and connected literature, trial and perturbation resources
records.outputs: Tool-grounded analyses, figures, cell-type-resolved repurposing predictions and cited syntheses with parameter logs
records.notes: System from the LungMAP Data Coordination Center at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center. A supervisor agent splits a natural-language question into parallel, tool-grounded tasks across single-cell and spatial analysis, literature and clinical-trial retrieval and drug repurposing, and can run custom Python or R code in a sandbox; its DART module separates perturbations that reverse disease programs from those that reinforce them at cell-type level. From a single prompt it planned and ran a six-step idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis analysis that ranked saracatinib first, a compound already evaluated in the STOP-IPF trial, and a separate query recovered fluticasone propionate for COPD; both are computational prioritisations without new experimental validation. Evaluation used an author-built set of 100 test cases, including adversarial queries, scored by code checks and a GPT-4o judge. Use is user-initiated and conversational. The hosted service is free for research use but requires LungMAP sign-in and caps queries per user; the production codebase is not released and reproducibility materials are available on request.

records.name: PromptBio
records.domain: End-to-end computational biomedical research on a hosted platform
records.inputs: Natural-language research objectives with user-supplied or platform-retrieved public datasets, optionally with organization-provided scripts or pipelines
records.outputs: Reviewable analysis plans; executed analyses with retained code, parameters, environment details, outputs and logs; tables, figures and evidence-grounded written syntheses
records.notes: Commercial hosted platform from PromptBio Inc. Its agent harness, PromptGenie, turns a research objective into a reviewable multi-step plan, delegates to subagents and skills (omics pipelines, statistics, machine learning, literature and database retrieval, nf-core and organization-supplied pipelines, generated Python/R/shell code), runs steps in sandboxed environments and revises the plan after failures or new results. The preprint compares PromptGenie with Biomni and STELLA on PromptBio-Bench, the company's own 244-task benchmark, and with Biomni and Noah.bio on the 12-task Health subset of DeepResearch Bench II; it also reports vendor validation of selected omics and machine-learning skills and a HAQER regulatory-genomics case study in which a researcher confirmed the analysis plan before execution. All authors are company employees, and the underlying language models were not matched across the compared systems. No public code; access is through a sign-in portal with a free trial and paid tiers. ToolsGenie 2.0 (asa-toolsgenie-2-0) comes from the same company, and its preprint states that it is available on the PromptBio platform.

records.name: SynAgent (autonomous thin-film synthesis)
records.domain: Hypothesis-driven autonomous thin-film materials synthesis

access_evidence.software_license: MIT

records.inputs: Campaign configuration (overview, target variable, allowed condition grid, fixed conditions), an OpenAI API key, and XRD patterns and SEM images delivered as MaiML files by an automated deposition and characterization platform
records.outputs: Proposed synthesis conditions with hypotheses and predictions, self-written analysis skills, synthesized films, and an explicit, revisable written understanding of the process
records.notes: Authors from the University of Tokyo, Rigaku and Mitsui Knowledge Industry replaced the Bayesian-optimization decision layer of the dLab automated thin-film platform with multimodal LLM agents (OpenAI Agents SDK, GPT-5.5). In one 18-experiment RF-sputtering campaign on LiCoO2 (001) films, the agents chose substrate temperatures, wrote their own XRD and SEM analysis skills and alternated proposals predicted to succeed and to fail. The paper states the films were synthesized and characterized without human intervention and describes no approval gate. Closure covered one controllable variable on a preset temperature grid with a fixed iteration budget. The paper offers code and data on request; the first author's MIT-licensed repository holds a cleaned port of the decision-layer code whose example settings differ from the published campaign, and the physical loop requires dLab. Unrelated to the humanoid-manipulation SynAgent (arXiv 2604.18557).

records.name: FermiLink
records.domain: Multidomain scientific simulation harness with an experimental-loop mode (autonomous quantum-transport measurements)
records.inputs: Markdown goal files, package knowledge bases for 150+ scientific codes or experimental skill repositories, an external coding agent (Codex, Claude Code, Gemini or OpenCode), laptop, HPC or lab-control workstation
records.outputs: Multi-day simulation and measurement campaigns, figure and paper reproductions, optimized scientific code, campaign memory and reports
records.notes: Harness from Tao E. Li's group (University of Delaware) that separates package knowledge bases from workflows and drives external coding agents. With Codex, its paper covers about 50 packages in nine domains and reproduces 74 of 132 published figures; a single-blinded test gave research-grade results on unpublished polariton problems when given detailed objectives and source code. A September 2026 preprint used its exploop mode to run cryogenic quantum-transport campaigns on MoS2 devices lasting up to six days without human intervention. Safety gate: all hardware access goes through a frozen acquisition script with hard-coded limits the agent cannot change; experts pre-build decision-tree Agent Skills for each device type, and the authors describe the autonomy as executing and adapting expert-defined workflows. The exploop code is in the AGPL-3.0 repository; the MoS2 transport skill repository named in its tutorial was not publicly reachable.

records.name: CAFES
aliases: Correlation-Aware Agentic Framework for Electronic Structure
records.domain: Agentic many-body electronic-structure simulation of strongly correlated systems
records.inputs: Natural-language or structured study/task requests; molecular geometries, POSCAR/CIF crystal structures or model-Hamiltonian lattices; local, Slurm or SSH-to-Slurm compute
records.outputs: Validated study and task specifications, generated PySCF input scripts, executed many-body calculations, correlation diagnostics, structured task/study reports with plots, and labelled datasets
records.notes: Rutgers University framework built on PySCF, with Block2, libDMET and fcDMFT for DMRG, DMET and DMFT, that organises calculations into studies and tasks. LLMs assist study planning and result interpretation; diagnostic-based method routing, validation, recovery and execution follow predefined rules, and the released package also runs without an LLM. Demonstrations: DMRG-CASSCF ground and low-lying excited states of lutein, adaptive DMET parameter scans of the extended honeycomb Hubbard model, and a CCSD-labelled dataset built from QM9 molecules. Active-space selection, refinements and other consequential steps require human approval. Apache-2.0 release with web, CLI, Python API and MCP interfaces.

records.name: CP-Agent
records.domain: Crystal-plasticity simulation workflows (PRISMS-Plasticity, CP-FEM and Taylor models)
records.inputs: One-sentence natural-language goal; typed CP tool set and optimizers; experimental or published reference stress-strain curves and target textures
records.outputs: Calibrated slip-hardening parameters, forward stress-strain/texture validations, recovered initial textures, chained five-pass rolling simulations, pole figures and visible reasoning traces
records.notes: ReAct-style GPT-4o agent from the University of Michigan (Aerospace Engineering). The harness is a minimal system prompt, typed tool schemas, a dispatcher and a safety-bounded iteration loop; numerical search is delegated to established optimizers. The same harness runs four case studies: SS316L calibration, OFHC copper forward validation and inverse texture recovery, and five-pass ZX31 magnesium rolling. Closure is computational only. The MIT-licensed code needs PRISMS-Plasticity, a commercial MATLAB licence with MTEX, and a paid LLM API. Different system from CrystalPlasticitySim and from unrelated arXiv systems also named CP-Agent (constraint programming, competitive programming, cell morphological profiling).

records.name: XRDreader
aliases: Experiment Reader Agentic Framework for X-Ray Diffraction
records.domain: Literature extraction of experimental powder-XRD figures and metadata
records.inputs: Search keywords, open-access publications (arXiv, Elsevier, Springer, CrossRef) and an LLM provider API key
records.outputs: Validated per-paper JSON records linking identified XRD figures to figure-level, text-derived and methodological metadata (no numerical digitisation of the patterns)
records.notes: Multi-agent pipeline by authors from the University of Rochester, NIST and other institutions that downloads and screens papers, identifies XRD figures, extracts and links metadata, and checks outputs against source evidence with an independent validation agent plus deterministic checks. On a curated 273-publication benchmark the paper reports up to 98.7% accuracy for XRD figure identification and 98.5% precision and 90.7% recall for the validated records. It does not yet digitise numerical diffraction data from figures. BSD-3-Clause code; benchmark data CC BY 4.0 on Zenodo. The README says the project was renamed from ERAF4XRD and will move to the DiffAI organisation. It builds databases rather than running experiments or simulations.

records.name: Rachel
records.domain: LLM-directed multistep retrosynthesis
records.inputs: Target molecule (SMILES), optional user priorities or constraints, and a host tool-capable general-purpose LLM agent
records.outputs: Multistep retrosynthetic route trees with sandbox-checked (RDKit) transformations, terminal precursor lists, planning and revision records, and route/reaction reports
records.notes: Stateful retrosynthesis-planning environment from the Hangzhou Institute of Medicine (Chinese Academy of Sciences), Beijing University of Chemical Technology and collaborators. A general-purpose LLM proposes and revises disconnections and chooses terminal precursors; Rachel executes candidate transformations in an RDKit-based sandbox and returns validation feedback, which the authors call a demonstration-level check that does not establish experimental feasibility. With GPT-5.5 the paper reports strict closure (complete route plus a separate post-hoc source audit of every terminal) for 111 of 120 PaRoutes targets and 24 of 25 RF25 targets. Planning is computational only: no laboratory synthesis was performed, route quality was scored by LLM evaluators, and RF25 routes had no human-expert review. Code and route atlas are CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); the README also links a login-gated web service.

access_evidence.software_license: CC-BY-NC-4.0

records.name: MADE
records.domain: Closed-loop computational materials-discovery environments
records.inputs: Discovery agents or algorithms composed of generators, planners, scorers and filters (or an LLM orchestrator with tools); convex-hull task definitions for a chemical system; an oracle and an evaluation budget
records.outputs: Discovery efficacy and efficiency metrics for simulated campaigns (AF, EF, AUDC, mSUN) and discovered stable structures
records.notes: Benchmark environments from Diffractive Labs, the University of Oxford and Imperial College London (ICML 2026 poster per the arXiv comment). MADE simulates budgeted closed-loop campaigns in which an agent or algorithm proposes, evaluates and refines candidate materials, with discovery framed as finding thermodynamically stable compounds relative to a convex hull. Policies range from fixed pipelines of generators, planners and filters to a ReAct-style LLM orchestrator with tools, compared with baseline algorithms. The oracle is an ML interatomic potential (ORB, MACE) or an analytic function; DFT or experimental oracles are named as future work, so campaigns are computational only. MIT-licensed official repository; setup uses a Materials Project API key.

records.name: AutoMat (computational-materials reproduction benchmark)
aliases: Can Coding Agents Reproduce Findings in Computational Materials Science?
records.domain: Reproducing claims from computational materials-science papers
records.inputs: Expert-curated claim from a computational materials-science paper, with paper text (paywalled PDFs supplied by the user), metadata and, where available, author-provided code or data; the coding agent under test
records.outputs: Agent execution trace, generated artifacts and analysis report on whether the evidence supports the claim; LLM-judge reproducibility score (1-5, success = score of 4 or more) calibrated against SME judgments
records.notes: Johns Hopkins benchmark (COLM 2026) of 85 claims curated by subject-matter experts, in three regimes: from paper text, from released artifacts, and interpretation of provided outputs. Five agent settings were evaluated: a task-specific orchestrated agent, Claude Code (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Kimi K2.5) and Codex CLI (GPT-5.4); the best reached a 53% success rate. Execution is computational only. Harness code is MIT. Claims are distributed separately as a gated Hugging Face dataset tagged CC BY 4.0, whose access form requires manual approval and agreement to non-commercial research use; 74 claims from 7 papers are released, others withheld pending publication, and paywalled papers are not included. Different system from the existing 'AutoMat' record (asa-automat-stem2mat-bench), a STEM microscopy-to-structure pipeline.

access_evidence.software_license: MIT harness code; benchmark claims on Hugging Face tagged CC-BY-4.0 but gated (manual approval) with a mandatory agreement to non-commercial research use; paywalled source papers not redistributed

records.name: AutoMOOSE
records.domain: Agentic phase-field (MOOSE) microstructure simulation
records.inputs: Natural-language phase-field simulation request; MOOSE installation with a registered physics plugin (grain growth or spinodal decomposition); LLM endpoint (Claude API or self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model); local or HPC compute
records.outputs: Generated MOOSE input files, executed simulations, screening and physics-falsification verdicts, kinetics analyses, visualizations, and provenance/recovery records
records.notes: Six-agent framework (Architect, Input Writer, Runner, Reviewer, Visualization, physics-grounded Skeptic) from University of Illinois Chicago and Argonne's Center for Nanoscale Materials. On a prospectively specified 25-task copper grain-growth benchmark it wrote valid inputs for all 25 tasks, 19 runs showed measurable coarsening, and 15 passed Burke-Turnbull kinetics and Skeptic falsification; a conserved Fe-Cr spinodal case is also shown. Automatic recovery changes only numerical settings, stops after three attempts, and asks the user to confirm unknown or low-confidence failures; repaired runs must pass the Skeptic again. In-silico only. Distinct from the existing MooseAgent and MOOSE-Chem records.

records.name: OpenAI4S
records.domain: Code-as-action computational research across chemistry, biology and materials science
records.inputs: Natural-language research requests, user data, bundled code skills, public-database connectors and a chosen model provider
records.outputs: Executed Python/R analyses, versioned artifacts, action ledgers, reports and resumable research sessions
records.notes: Research agent from Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School (PKU-YuanGroup) with Beijing Yuankong Intelligent Technology; the README credits the Peking University-YuanKong Intelligence AI Joint Research Laboratory. The name stands for 'Open AI for Scientist' and does not denote an OpenAI product; the README presents it as an open-source reproduction of the Claude Science architecture. Structured tool calls handle orchestration and permissions while scientific actions run as code cells in persistent Python and R kernels, with an append-only action ledger, versioned artifacts and checkpoints. MIT. The paper scores 36 computational scenarios in chemistry, biology and materials science with an author-built evaluator. Gated operations use a permission broker; in keyword-triggered biosecurity screening only BLOCK stops execution, while ESCALATE is advisory and does not wait for a human decision. No laboratory loop is demonstrated.

records.name: AutoResearchClaw
records.domain: Idea-to-paper autonomous computational research with optional human co-piloting
records.inputs: A research idea or topic, model/agent backend configuration and local compute (GPU/MPS/CPU) with a Docker sandbox
records.outputs: Literature-grounded hypotheses, sandboxed experiment code and results, verified citations and a LaTeX paper draft
records.notes: AIMING Lab (UNC-Chapel Hill) 23-stage pipeline: multi-agent debate for hypotheses and result analysis, a self-healing executor with a Pivot/Refine loop, checks of reported numbers and citations against executed outputs, and lessons carried across runs. MIT. Three gate stages wait for human approval unless auto-approve is set. In the paper, Full-Auto runs completed idea-to-paper on 8 of 10 topics, but targeted human input at key stages scored higher than full autonomy. The main benchmark is 25 ML topics, with a smaller extension in high-energy physics, systems biology and statistics. All experiments are computational. Distinct from AutoResearch (EvoMap), Karpathy's autoresearch and ResearchClawBench.

records.name: data-to-paper
records.domain: Autonomous data-driven research with backward-traceable manuscripts
records.inputs: Annotated datasets, an optional research goal and LLM API access; optional human co-pilot review
records.outputs: Research goals and hypotheses, analysis plans, debugged analysis code, tables, literature citations and complete manuscripts whose numbers are traced back to code and data
records.notes: Technion Kishony-lab platform that guides interacting LLM and rule-based agents through 17 predefined research steps, from annotated data via literature search (Semantic Scholar), hypothesis and analysis code to a manuscript whose numeric results are programmatically chained to code and data. Published in NEJM AI (2025); MIT. In the reported autopilot runs a user approved each research step (overseeing only). For simple goals the authors report manuscripts recapitulating peer-reviewed results without major errors in about 80-90% of runs; human co-piloting becomes critical as goal complexity increases. Statistical analysis of supplied data only; no new experiments are run.

records.name: ASI-Arch
aliases: AlphaGo Moment for Model Architecture Discovery
records.domain: Autonomous neural-architecture research (AI-for-AI)
records.inputs: An architecture research target, seed architecture and baseline, a user-supplied training/evaluation script, LLM API access, GPU compute, and the database and cognition-base services
records.outputs: Proposed and implemented architectures, training and benchmark results, analyses and an experiment database
records.notes: GAIR-NLP multi-agent loop (Researcher, Engineer, Analyzer, experience repository) that proposes, implements, trains and analyses linear-attention architectures, using an experiment database and a cognition base distilled from about 100 papers. The paper reports 1,773 autonomous experiments at 20M parameters; the authors then selected about 150 candidates for 340M verification (105 state-of-the-art; the repository lists 106) and 5 for 1.3B validation. The Apache-2.0 release includes the pipeline, both services and the discovered architectures; the training script must be supplied by the user. Closure is computational and GPU-intensive. Separate system from the later GAIR-NLP ASI-Evolve. The repository keeps the v1 title 'AlphaGo Moment for Model Architecture Discovery'; the current arXiv title is 'Neural Architecture Discovery via Autonomous Evolution'.

records.name: OpenEvolve
records.domain: Open evolutionary coding agent for program, algorithm and mathematical discovery
records.inputs: An initial program, an evaluator that scores candidates, and LLM backend configuration
records.outputs: Evolved programs and their evaluation scores across iterations
records.notes: Evolutionary coding agent created by Asankhaya Sharma (GitHub codelion), now hosted by the Algorithmic SuperIntelligence Labs organisation and described in its repository as an open-source implementation of AlphaEvolve. Apache-2.0. An LLM ensemble proposes code changes, a user-supplied evaluator scores them, and a MAP-Elites program database with islands decides which programs are kept. It is an independent reimplementation and is separate from Google DeepMind's AlphaEvolve. No primary paper was found; the README asks users to cite it as software. Papers from 2026 use it as a baseline or search harness for discovery agents. Independent groups have applied it to combinatorial bijection construction and to Zarankiewicz-number bounds. The user defines the problem, initial program and evaluator. The loop then closes computationally, with no physical loop.

records.name: ARK (idea2paper.org)
records.domain: Idea-to-paper research automation with computational experiments; example outputs in machine-learning and systems research

paper_links.label: ICML 2026 AI for Science workshop poster

records.inputs: A research idea or proposal PDF, a target venue template, user-supplied model API keys, and local, Slurm or SkyPilot cloud compute
records.outputs: Literature survey, experiment code and results, venue-formatted LaTeX paper and iterative AI review reports
records.notes: Multi-agent idea-to-paper system from SANDS Lab, KAUST (repository kaust-ark/ARK, service at idea2paper.org). Agents for research, planning, coding, experiments, writing and review take a project from proposal analysis and literature search through local, Slurm or SkyPilot cloud experiments to a venue-formatted LaTeX paper; an AI reviewer scores each draft and the revision loop repeats until a score threshold. Apache-2.0 and self-hostable; the hosted instance runs on the user's own model API keys. Before risky actions such as deletions, cloud provisioning or crossing a spend cap it can ask for Telegram approval, but with no Telegram configured it auto-allows and logs them; an ethics-and-soundness gate screens ideas before launch. Described in an ICML 2026 AI for Science workshop poster. Example outputs are ML and systems papers; a study co-authored by one ARK developer also ran it on five ResearchClawBench tasks in neuroscience, energy, life science and physics. Not the same system as AgentAlphaAGI's Idea2Paper (Idea2Story).

records.name: ScienceBuddy
records.domain: Interactive biomedical research workspace with self-improving agent harness and model
records.inputs: Researcher questions with papers, tables, biological sequences or scientific images
records.outputs: Evidence tables, study plans, presentations and other generated files, with inspectable tool and code-execution trajectories
records.notes: PhAI Labs hosted workspace in which a ReAct-style agent with 224 mostly biomedical tools plans, retrieves literature and database records, and runs Python, R or Bash code; researchers direct and refine the work in conversation and can inspect each tool call. The paper couples harness evolution with GRPO model training ('recursive-in-recursive self-improvement'); in the reported runs an external frontier model proposes harness edits and user feedback is simulated, on LAB-Bench and Biomni-Eval1 tasks. Workspace case studies are qualitative, translated recordings. The public MIT repository contains only a simplified agent (Simple-SciBuddy) and the self-improvement experiment code; the hosted product source is excluded and hosted-preview access terms are not stated.

records.name: Quailbot
records.domain: Agentic scanning tunneling microscopy and instrument operation
records.inputs: Instrument workspace definitions, CLI instrument drivers and natural-language task prompts
records.outputs: Instrument actions with linked readbacks, experiment logs, agent completion reports and measurement-ready STM tips
records.notes: Boston College harness, released as an ISC-licensed Pi extension, that places frontier LLMs inside an STM feedback loop by returning linked readbacks after every instrument action. After a human apprenticeship, launch-prompt-only runs with two frontier models conditioned tungsten tips on FeTe at 4 K to lattice-resolving endpoints without further human messages; a human STM expert verified endpoints afterwards. Disclosed gates: state-changing tools are denied unless the operator enables them with a launch-time environment flag, and piezo-voltage control was withheld for safety. A bent tip, a hidden walker jam and an exhausted sample area needed human disclosure or physical intervention. The demonstrated task is tip conditioning, not a full scientific campaign; workspaces, prompts, transcripts and STM data are promised on Zenodo upon publication.

records.name: Solver Agent
records.domain: Agentic calculations and proofs in mathematics and theoretical physics
records.inputs: Researcher-posed problems in mathematics or theoretical physics; an LLM provider API key (OpenAI by default) and MongoDB; optional Wolfram Engine, CYTools and C++ compiler
records.outputs: Append-only ledgers of assumptions, derivations, code, outputs and verifier verdicts; answers released after LLM full-solution review; exportable HTML, LaTeX and JSON session records
records.notes: AGPL-3.0-or-later system by Eliott Morgensztern. A coordinating solver delegates to symbolic and numerical sub-agents, with optional Calabi-Yau (CYTools) and web-literature sub-agents, and logs every step in an append-only ledger; separate LLM verifier agents must accept the full solution before an answer is released. The accompanying paper applies it to global F-theory uplifts of O3-planes and S-folds. The researchers wrote and sometimes split each prompt; one session derived the conditions for Theorem 4.2 without follow-up input. Verification is LLM-based and gives no formal proof-assistant certificate. Requires a paid LLM API.

records.name: LaMET-Agent
records.domain: Lattice QCD large-momentum effective theory (LaMET) analysis
records.inputs: Lattice correlator data (HDF5 with JSON descriptors) and a JSON/JSONC analysis manifest declaring the stage job graph, optionally completed through an LLM planning dialogue
records.outputs: Light-cone parton distribution functions and distribution amplitudes as NetCDF artifacts, with fit diagnostics, plots, per-stage reports and a final literature-grounded review report
records.notes: MIT-licensed Python framework that runs a LaMET lattice-QCD analysis as a manifest-declared job graph: correlator analysis, renormalization, Fourier transform, perturbative matching, continuum/pion-mass/infinite-momentum extrapolation, and review. All numerics run in deterministic tools. The LLM is used at three points: an optional planning dialogue that ends with explicit user acceptance of the manifest, bounded and validated choices of fit windows and ranges inside stages, and a final review against the literature that leaves results unchanged. The authors report four end-to-end reproductions (pion PDFs in gauge-invariant and Coulomb-gauge formulations, pion and kaon distribution amplitudes) consistent with published calculations; comparisons across LLM providers, against expert baselines and across repeated runs are still open. Works with a logged-in Codex CLI or with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek or OpenAI-compatible APIs. The release covers collinear quark distributions; example data come from a separate password-protected host with a self-signed certificate.

records.name: QIQCBench / Quantum-Harbor
records.domain: Verified autonomy of AI agents in quantum engineering (simulated hardware)
records.inputs: Agent harnesses (e.g., Codex CLI, Claude Code, OpenCode) and containerized task bundles with public device specifications and lab notebooks
records.outputs: Pass/fail verdicts and Elo racing ratings per task and agentic system, graded against logged experiment evidence
records.notes: Benchmark of 49 expert-authored quantum-engineering tasks run in Quantum-Harbor, a Harbor-based virtual laboratory where agents reach simulated devices with hidden parameters through MCP tools and a separate verifier grades submissions against the logged experiment evidence. The paper evaluates 17 agentic systems. The MIT repository, published by the authors under GaugeForge (a co-author affiliation), releases the framework and five task bundles; the other 44 tasks are not public, so the reported results cannot be fully reproduced. All released tasks run on simulators; the code has an opt-in IBM Quantum live backend, but no hardware run is reported.

records.name: AstroGenesis
records.domain: Multi-agent astrophysics research platform (blazars; multiwavelength and multimessenger data, SED modelling)
records.inputs: Natural-language astrophysics research questions about a source; optionally user-uploaded data files or documents
records.outputs: Literature syntheses with cited references, retrieved multiwavelength light curves and SEDs (plots, CSV), surrogate-based broadband model fits with best-fit parameters, and up to five ranked candidate research directions
records.notes: Hosted beta platform (free tier of 10 messages per day; paid Pro tier) from an ICRANet-Armenia-led team with international co-authors. A Supervisor Agent and a Planner/Replanner route each query through literature, data-retrieval, theoretical-modelling and research-ideation agents; the current module covers blazars only. The modelling agent fits SSC, EIC, hadronic and lepto-hadronic models with pretrained neural-network surrogates and Bayesian inference. Only literature retrieval is benchmarked (Hit@5 76.6% single-paper, 79.2% multi-paper); modelling and ideation are shown as worked examples. Runs are user-initiated per query. No source-code release was found.

records.name: SimuVerity
records.domain: Engineering-grade Simulink model generation by agents
records.inputs: 101 natural-language engineering specifications with delivery requirements, solved through MATLAB/Simulink MCP tools; evaluator-owned native simulation scenarios
records.outputs: Hierarchical scores for delivery, executability, engineering qualification and six quality dimensions
records.notes: Benchmark from Xi'an Jiaotong University: 101 text-to-Simulink tasks across ten engineering domains, scored by a hierarchical evaluator that runs native simulation scenarios. Six agent systems were evaluated in isolated sessions; the best overall score was 42.86. First-party code and result tables are Apache-2.0. Most bundled reference models are third-party assets under their own terms, some restricted to use with MathWorks products. Generating and evaluating candidates requires proprietary MATLAB R2025a and Simulink. Evaluation is computational simulation only.

records.name: Ansatz (mathematical research)
records.domain: Long-horizon mathematical research with continual graph memory
records.inputs: Mathematical research problems, operator-chosen worker roles and stop conditions, and optional cross-project research memory
records.outputs: Model-verifier-accepted proof records, exploration graphs, progress reports and research manuscripts
records.notes: Apache-2.0 release from UCLA (uclanlp), linked from the paper. It extends the Danus architecture (parallel proof workers, a separate verifier, a shared fact graph), and the LICENSE keeps the FrenzyMath copyright notice. A main agent coordinates workers, the verifier and a memory curator over a dependency-linked fact graph and an exploration graph, with optional cross-problem recall. A human operator supplies the problem and sets worker roles and stop conditions; live runs need an authenticated Claude Code CLI and a Codex backend. Acceptance is by model-based review only, with no proof-assistant certificate or independent expert grading. The paper reports 10/10 closures on First Proof Second Batch; the release notes record 9/10 in the archived run and one task resumed after a manual architecture switch.

records.name: QED (open-problem proof agent)
records.domain: Natural-language proof generation for research-level mathematical problems
records.inputs: LaTeX statements of research-level mathematical problems; Codex, Claude or Gemini CLI backends configured per agent role
records.outputs: Literature-survey notes, YAML proof plans, candidate proofs, structural and detailed verification reports, final natural-language proofs with citations and a proof-effort summary
records.notes: MIT-licensed pipeline from authors at UC San Diego, Caltech and AWS (work done outside Amazon). It runs a survey agent, a proof-plan decomposer, a prover, structural and detailed verifiers and a regulator that revises the proof, revises the plan or restarts. Codex is the default backend; Claude or Gemini can be set per role. The paper reports 18 open problems contributed by collaborating mathematicians; on five projects, run without human guidance, those experts judged QED's proofs correct and original (probability, algebraic geometry, fluid PDEs, inverse problems). Optional human steering exists but was not used. Checking is done by language models, not a proof assistant, so outputs need expert review.

records.name: GW-Eyes
records.domain: Gravitational-wave electromagnetic-counterpart association (multi-messenger astronomy)
records.inputs: GW posterior samples and skymaps (e.g. GWTC-4.0), EM event catalogs, GCN circulars, and natural-language task requests
records.outputs: Candidate GW-EM counterpart lists with reports, updated local event database, skymap and luminosity-distance visualizations, and logged tool-call reasoning traces
records.notes: Peking University LLM agent framework with two sub-agents. The Collector pulls GCN circulars and catalogs, extracts event properties and applies rule-based and self-consistency checks. The Executor plans and runs MCP-integrated tools for GW-EM association, in both directions (GW to EM and EM to GW), plus skymap visualization and rapid verification. Tasks are human-initiated. It was evaluated on simulated injections (50 GWTC-4.0 events) and applied to AGN flares (AGNFRC) and GWTC-4.0, with the associations manually cross-checked. Published in The Innovation (2026). Requires a user-supplied LLM API. MIT-licensed. Distinct from GWAgent.

records.name: SimulCost
records.domain: Cost-aware LLM-agent parameter tuning for physics simulations
records.inputs: Simulation tasks (2,643 single-round, 2,304 multi-round) naming a solver, a tunable parameter and an accuracy requirement; multi-round mode allows up to 10 simulator calls
records.outputs: Proposed parameter values with convergence and cost feedback traces, scored for success rate and computational cost against brute-force scanning and Bayesian-optimization baselines
records.notes: Benchmark from the Rose-STL-Lab group at UC San Diego. LLMs tune solver parameters for 12 simulators across fluid dynamics, heat transfer, solid mechanics and plasma physics. In single-round mode the model makes one guess. In multi-round mode it works by trial and error over up to 10 simulator calls, with convergence and cost feedback after each call. Cost is counted analytically for 11 simulators; the production plasma code EPOCH is timed by wall clock and reported separately. The benchmark harness and Hugging Face dataset are Apache-2.0. The required solver library (the first author's simulcost-tools submodule) has no licence file. According to the v4 arXiv comment, CGYRO was removed because of a bug and will be added back. All evaluation is computational simulation.

access_evidence.software_license: Apache-2.0 benchmark harness (Rose-STL-Lab/SimulCost-Bench) and Hugging Face dataset; required solver submodule Eydcao/simulcost-tools has no licence file at verification (2026-10-10), nor do its nested fem_transient_utils and CSMPM_BOW submodules; bundled third-party EPOCH is GPL-3.0

records.name: HEPLocalAgent
records.domain: Local natural-language construction and execution of collider simulation workflows
records.inputs: Plain-language collider simulation requests; a user-selected local language model served through Ollama and a routing profile
records.outputs: Validated MadGraph, Pythia8 and Delphes inputs presented for expert approval; after approval, locally executed simulation runs with output checks and a JSON run record (commands, cross section, return code)
records.notes: MIT-licensed local interface from the Indian Institute of Science (Aadarsh Singh, Sudhir K. Vempati). A locally served model proposes a typed workflow; deterministic code restores recognized user-stated quantities, builds and validates inputs for MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, Pythia8, Delphes and a restricted MadAnalysis 5 plan, with a bounded repair loop. Every workflow passes a human approval gate before execution. In the paper, 4 of 7 approved workflows ran to completion, and natural-language routing to MadAnalysis was not demonstrated. The authors describe v1.0.1 as a validation-gated workflow constructor that needs expert approval, not an autonomous agent. External HEP tools keep their own licences.

records.name: ADMET-EvO
aliases: ADMET-EvO: a self-evolving scientific agent for sustained research across heterogeneous tasks
records.domain: Self-evolving ADMET and toxicity prediction research for small molecules
records.inputs: ADMET endpoint definitions, TDC benchmark training/validation splits and optionally curated external assay data
records.outputs: Hypothesis-tagged experiment ledgers, frozen model configurations, multi-seed test scores and endpoint-specific predictors
records.notes: Authors are affiliated with Valhalla Technology, CUHK, Zhejiang University and Stanford University. A language-model planning policy proposes falsifiable hypotheses and picks data, feature or model interventions; a separate deterministic evaluator and update rule assign supported, rejected or inconclusive verdicts. The paper reports 22 TDC ADMET tasks and an expansion to 43 toxicity tasks, listed in the repository's Table S2 as ToxCast endpoints. The MIT-licensed repository (v0.3.0) uses a local rule-based planner by default with an optional OpenAI-compatible LLM planner, and external data enter training only after recorded scientific review. All closure is computational; no laboratory validation is reported.

records.name: SolutionsX
aliases: SolutionsX: supergravity theories/solutions as code, with an agentic workflow for machine-verifiable physics
records.domain: Machine-verifiable supergravity and tensor-geometry records with an agent toolkit
