scope.note: In scope as a benchmark/harness that evaluates closed-loop scientific agents: multi-round perturbation selection against a hidden oracle with true/random/no-feedback conditions, plus a trace evaluator for Feedback-to-State, State-to-Action and Action-to-Outcome. Reusable (17 task manifests + CLI harness), so not a one-off case-study audit. Note: closure is in-silico replay of public screen data; the authors' Limitations state the hidden hit sets are effect thresholds on public measurements and may be recoverable from prior knowledge.

autonomy.note: B is correct (benchmark/harness). No physical or new-experiment loop; oracle feedback is replayed from existing screens.

Caveats to disclose in notes (do not change access): (a) README release-status says this is the research benchmark and evaluation harness, with a fuller release planned 'over the next few months'; (b) the Chef_Harness runtime adapter is Codex CLI only (runtimes/: __init__.py, codex.py); the paper's non-agent comparators (random, active learning, LLM-guided BO) and the BioDiscoveryAgent/Biomni adapters were not found in the 168-file public tree; (c) the repo ships normalised hidden oracle scores and hit sets derived from third-party resources (GDSC, DepMap, Project DRIVE, JUMP, published screens), whose upstream terms are separate from MIT (e.g. GDSC provenance file records 'public GDSC download page'); (d) task_index.yaml declares task_count 20 while 17 task manifests are shipped (the 17 match the paper). Paper text itself is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, irrelevant to code access.

text.note: Notes understate and partly misdescribe the task suite: '17 tasks built from CRISPR and CRISPRa screens in primary T cells, CAR-T, NK cells and tau or choline biology' omits RNAi (Project DRIVE), DepMap/Achilles dependency, GDSC2 small-molecule drug response and JUMP Cell Painting morphology tasks; paper section 3.2 says the tasks span knockout, activation, RNA interference, small-molecule treatment and morphology screening. 'Underlying screen data come from the original public sources' is inaccurate for the repo: raw source files are not shipped, but normalised per-candidate oracle scores and hit sets are. The comparators (active learning, LLM-guided BO) are reported in the paper but not present in the public repo; the notes should not imply the release includes them. No exact-name match in asa_identity.tsv or asa_deprecated_ids.json. MISSED RELATION: the proposal gives matched_existing_id null, but the catalog already holds asa-toolsgenie-2-0 (ToolsGenie 2.0, paper-only), whose preprint is from the same company and corresponding author and states 'ToolsGenie 2.0 is available on the PromptBio platform (platform.promptbio.ai).' The 2025 PromptBio platform preprint (10.1101/2025.07.05.663295) describes ToolsGenie as one of PromptBio's analysis modes. The 2026 PromptBio paper does not mention ToolsGenie. This is a component/umbrella overlap, not a rename or same-name collision: PromptBio is the umbrella platform, PromptGenie its agent harness, ToolsGenie a code-generation component. Default: add PromptBio as its own platform record (as the catalog does for Edison components: Kosmos, platform agents, PaperQA3) and cross-reference ToolsGenie 2.0 in notes. Follow-up for the baseline record, outside this addition: asa-toolsgenie-2-0 is labelled paper-only although its own abstract says it is available on the PromptBio platform, so its access should be re-checked (likely platform). Alias fix: OmicsGenie is the omics-pipeline skill set inside PromptBio (Section 3), not another name for the platform, so it should be removed from aliases. PromptGenie stays as an alias because the paper presents it as the agent harness at the platform's centre.

scope.note: In scope. The harness plans multi-step biomedical research, combines literature and database retrieval, public-data discovery, omics pipelines, statistics, machine learning and generated Python/R/shell code, executes steps in sandboxed environments and revises the plan after failures or new results (Sections 2.1-2.4). Evaluated end to end on PromptBio-Bench and DeepResearch Bench II Health subset, plus a hypothesis-driven HAQER case study (Section 5). Not a general LLM, a single pipeline or a business agent.

autonomy.note: A3 supported by observed closure: in the benchmarks the agent completed tasks end to end with generated scripts; in the HAQER case study it inspected inputs, proposed a plan, received researcher confirmation, then generated and executed the full workflow and returned code, tables and figures. All closure is computational; no laboratory loop, so A5 does not apply. A4 is not supported: research questions and hypotheses came from researchers, and the authors state the evaluations do not establish 'fully autonomous research settings'. Human gate to disclose: researchers review and confirm the plan (Section 2.5; Figure 5a caption).

identity.note: Both preprints resolve on arXiv (2604.03460 v1 2026-04-03, v2 2026-04-07; 2609.26661 v1 2026-09-22), no withdrawal notice, titles/authors match. Tao E. Li (University of Delaware) is last author of the framework paper and co-corresponding author of the transport paper; the transport paper states its workflow is implemented through the FermiLink harness and cites 2604.03460. Repository TaoELi/FermiLink is owned by Tao E. Li's GitHub account (bio: Assistant Professor, Physics and Astronomy, University of Delaware), is linked in the arXiv comment field, and its README cites the arXiv paper; fermilink.org is the repo homepage and README-linked docs. Not a fork. No baseline match; the only 'Fermi*' baseline record is FERMIACC (asa-fermiacc, arXiv 2603.22538, Agrawal/Craig et al., particle theory), a different system. arXiv full-text search for 'FermiLink' returns only these two papers. Correction: drop alias 'codex-fermilink'. It is a separate Apache-2.0 fork of openai/codex (TaoELi/codex-fermilink, npm @tel-research/codex-fermilink, first published 2026-08-31), a companion distribution and not a former or alternative name of the AGPL harness.

scope.note: Multi-step scientific work: goal.md-driven multi-job simulation campaigns on workstation/HPC, figure- and paper-level reproduction, 'research' mode for paper-scale campaigns, code optimization, and an 'exploop' mode for iterative instrument-driven experiments. Not a base model or a single software component.

autonomy.note: A4-A5 is supported by observed closure. A4: 132-task reproduction benchmark plus a single-blinded study producing research-grade results on unpublished polariton problems (with human-supplied detailed objectives and source code). A5: 2609.26661 reports real dilution-refrigerator measurements at 10 mK on monolayer and bilayer MoS2 devices; the harness assigns measurement agents that design sweeps and submit them, polls instrument status, hands data to analysis agents that decide to proceed, redo or stop, over campaigns up to six days, including a negative-control low-quality device where the agent skipped steps. Disclosure required and missing from the proposal notes: hardware access is mediated by a frozen acquisition script with hard-coded limits (gate voltage, sweep rate, field, temperature); a human loads the device; expert-developed decision-tree Agent Skills with predefined sub-questions are needed per device type, refined by human-reviewed dry runs; authors state the autonomy 'primarily concerns the execution and adaptation of expert-defined experimental workflows'. These gates do not preclude A5 under MAINTENANCE.md but must be stated; corrected notes do so. Transport paper is an unrefereed v1 preprint.

access.note: open-source confirmed: GitHub REST licence endpoint spdx_id AGPL-3.0, path LICENSE; LICENSE content (fetched via the API-provided download_url) begins 'GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 19 November 2007'; README licence section 'AGPL-3.0'; PyPI fermilink 0.3.10 classifier 'License :: OSI Approved :: GNU Affero General Public License v3'. GitHub releases list only v0.2.1 (2026-04-07); PyPI and docs are at 0.3.10. The exploop harness code is public (src/fermilink/exploop/*). The experiment-specific MoS2 transport skills referenced in the exploop tutorial (github.com/skilled-quantum/skill-mos2-quantum-transport) return 404 via web and API; the skilled-quantum organization lists no public repositories. So the A5 harness is open-source, but the device-specific skills and frozen acquisition script used in the campaigns are not public; disclosed in notes. access_evidence null is acceptable for open-source.

category.note: crossdomain accepted. Fig. 2a of 2604.03460v2 lists nine benchmark domains: Robotics; Quantum Science and Technology; Materials Science and Photonics; Life Sciences and Neuroscience; High-Energy, Nuclear and Particle Physics; Engineering and Comp. Mechanics; Earth and Environmental Science; Chemistry and Molecular Science; Astronomy and Astrophysics. Coverage beyond the physical sciences (life sciences/neuroscience, robotics) supports crossdomain over physics, and the physics-engineering lane independently proposed crossdomain too. Correction: domain text 'physical-science' dropped since the benchmark includes life sciences.

(1) Proposal notes say the public repository documents 'simulation, reproduction and code-optimization modes' and that release of instrument-control skills 'was not verified'; the README lists a public 'exploop' experimental mode (added to docs 2026-05-17) and the MoS2 skill repo it names is 404, so this is now stated precisely. identity.note: Both preprints resolve (arXiv API, abs and HTML all 200): 2603.20986 (v1 2026-03-22, v2 2026-08-07; 'AutoMOOSE: An Agentic AI for Autonomous Phase-Field Simulation') and 2608.20571 v1 (2026-08-20; software/architecture-views paper). Same three authors on both (Sukriti Manna, Henry Chan, Subramanian K. R. S. Sankaranarayanan; UIC + Argonne CNM). No withdrawal text on either abs page. Repository github.com/sukritimanna/AutoMOOSE is author-owned (GitHub user profile: Sukriti Manna, Argonne National Laboratory) and is cited as the code location in both papers' code-availability sections; not a fork, not archived. Not a duplicate of baseline asa-mooseagent (different authors, repo taozhan18/MooseAgent, general MOOSE/FEM tasks) nor of asa-moose-chem/asa-moose-chem2 (chemistry hypothesis generation; name collision only on 'MOOSE'). Not in asa_deprecated_ids.json. Same-name collision outside the catalog: github.com/girba/automoose (2010, shell scripts for the Moose software-analysis platform) is unrelated; arXiv search for 'AutoMOOSE' returns only these two papers. PROCESS FLAG: the same system was proposed independently by the physics-engineering lane (category physics) and the chemistry-materials lane (category chemistry); decisions.json lists also_in physics-engineering. Merge into ONE record.

scope.note: Genuinely multi-step scientific work: natural-language request -> plan (Architect) -> MOOSE input generation -> execution/monitoring -> screening -> physics-grounded falsification (Skeptic) -> bounded recovery and re-run -> analysis/interpretation. Validated on a 25-task grain-growth benchmark, a 1000-run ensemble Arrhenius analysis and a Fe-Cr spinodal case. Not a generic library or one-off audit.

autonomy.note: A3 supported and not higher. Observed closure is an in-silico execution-diagnosis-recovery loop on user-specified tasks ('with no human intervention' on the 25-task benchmark). It does not choose research questions or generate hypotheses; Bayesian-optimisation 'active learning and autonomous discovery' is listed only as future work (2603.20986 Sec. 4.6.4), so A4 is not supported. Simulation/HPC only, so no A5 question. Human gate to disclose: recovery prompt requests user confirmation for UNKNOWN failures and for diagnoses with confidence < 0.7 (2603.20986 Supplementary S1.4); recovery is capped at 3 attempts and touches only numerical/discretization controls (README).

access.note: open-source confirmed. gh api repos/sukritimanna/AutoMOOSE/license: path LICENSE, spdx_id MIT, name 'MIT License'; decoded content and raw.githubusercontent.com LICENSE (200) both read 'MIT License / Copyright (c) 2026 Sukriti Manna, Henry Chan, and Subramanian Sankaranarayanan'. Both papers state MIT. Repo has a v1.0 tag but no GitHub Releases; the software paper describes v0.2.0 and says a Zenodo archive will be deposited on acceptance (none yet). Running it requires a MOOSE build and an LLM endpoint (Claude API or self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model).

category.note: Proposed 'chemistry'; correct to 'physics'. AutoMOOSE runs continuum phase-field (Allen-Cahn grain growth, Cahn-Hilliard spinodal decomposition) finite-element simulations in MOOSE; the closest catalog precedents are MooseAgent (MOOSE/FEM, physics), VFEAgent and MechAgents (FEM, physics), and the run guidance places materials-physics/engineering under physics while chemistry covers chemistry/materials synthesis/self-driving chemistry labs. arXiv primary class of the software paper is cond-mat.mtrl-sci (system paper: cs.AI with cond-mat.mes-hall). Contested-but-weaker alternative: chemistry via AtomAgents/DREAMS precedent (atomistic/DFT materials agents). The physics-engineering lane independently chose physics.

scope.note: Multi-step research pipeline: 23 stages covering literature retrieval and screening, hypothesis generation by multi-agent debate, experiment design, code generation, sandboxed execution with repair, result analysis, a Proceed/Refine/Pivot decision loop, and LaTeX paper writing with citation verification. autonomy.note: A4 supported by observed closure: the paper's end-to-end HITL ablation (Table 3) runs Full-Auto mode with 0 interventions from idea to paper on 10 topics, 8/10 valid, mean quality 4.03/10, 25% LLM-judge accept; the ARC-Bench experiment-stage run also reports a Full-Auto row (0.596 overall). All experiments are computational (Docker sandbox; HEP via MadGraph/Delphes, systems biology via COBRApy, statistics simulations), so A5 does not apply. Disclose the human gates: README says gate stages 5, 9 and 20 pause for human approval unless --auto-approve is set, and the authors' own ablation finds targeted human input (CoPilot, 7.27/10) beats Full-Auto. The proposed note already states the ablation finding; the corrected note adds the gate default and the Full-Auto result.

README citation block names Sharma as author. No primary paper exists: an arXiv title search for 'OpenEvolve' returned only a third-party application paper (2511.20987), so the record correctly has no paper_links. No catalog collision: 'openevolve' does not appear in the baseline identity TSV, the deprecated IDs, or any Autonomous_Agents file. It is separate from asa-alphaevolve (DeepMind, results-only repo) and must not be merged with it. Small unrelated GitHub repos share the name (e.g. jamesahou/openevolve with 8 stars, gratitude5dee/OpenEvolve, ryanrudes/openevolve), plus many forks or copies of the canonical repo. The repo URL disambiguates, so no display-name change is needed.

scope.note: This is the weakest point, but the record passes. OpenEvolve is a generic LLM-driven program optimiser, and the protocol excludes 'optimization libraries'. Most README showcases are engineering tasks (function minimisation, GPU kernels, sorting, web scraping). Three things count against exclusion. (a) Direct catalog precedent: ShinkaEvolve (asa-shinkaevolve, A3, Apache-2.0, user-supplied evaluator) was admitted on 2026-08-13, and AlphaEvolve is catalogued. Rejecting the most-used open member of this class would be inconsistent. (b) Third-party papers frame it as a discovery or research agent: arXiv 2607.18235 calls it an 'autonomous discovery system', and 2609.26457 benchmarks it as one of six AI research agents alongside AI Scientist and AIDE. (c) Independent scientific use exists: combinatorial bijection discovery (2511.20987) and new Zarankiewicz-number bounds (2605.01120). The multi-step loop is: LLM proposes code edits, the evaluator executes and scores, MAP-Elites/island selection follows, and the cycle repeats.

autonomy.note: A3 is supported and matches ShinkaEvolve. The user supplies the problem framing, the initial program, the evaluator and the config/system prompt. The evolutionary loop then runs without humans and closes computationally only. There is no literature, hypothesis or physical loop, so A4 and A5 are not warranted. The README's 'No human guidance needed' slogan describes the inner loop only.

identity.note: arXiv 2609.27302v1 (23 Sep 2026, cond-mat.mes-hall; Cheng, Xu, Candelora, Zeljkovic, Boston College) resolves via abs page (200), HTML (200) and arXiv API; only v1, no withdrawal notice. Paper names the system 'quailbot' and its Data availability section gives https://github.com/BB-84C/quailbot-pi; its references hyperlink https://github.com/BB-84C/quail-cli-core and BB-84C/NanonisSPMController-CLI. GitHub user BB-84C = 'Siyu Cheng', company 'Boston College' (first and corresponding author), so both repos are author-owned. No baseline match (grep on quail/STM/tunneling/probe/instrument/BB-84C/2609.27302 in asa_identity.tsv; nothing in asa_deprecated_ids.json); not proposed by another lane. Same-name check: gh search finds only unrelated 'QuailBot' repos (a Discord bot, a React Native dialer), none in the catalog. Nearest catalog neighbours (TEM Agent, CALMS, NV-center agent, Vibe Calibration, k-agents) are different systems. Alias correction: the paper expands 'quail' (not 'Quailbot') as Quantum Uncertain Action-Outcome Instrument Loop; the released software is named 'Quailbot Pi' (release titles, package @bb84/quailbot-pi).

scope.note: Multi-step experimental work on a real low-temperature STM: the agent issues bias pulses, tip shakes, coarse piezo walks and scans, reads back live topographs and revises its plan. Tip conditioning is instrument preparation, not a full research campaign; this is in scope by catalog precedent for instrument-operation agents (Vibe Calibration, k-agents, CALMS, TEM Agent), and the proposed notes already say so.

autonomy.note: A3-A5 supported and consistent with TEM Agent and Accelerator Assistant precedents. Observed physical closure: two launch-prompt-only runs with two frontier models received a task prompt and operated 'without further human messages until its terminal report', delivering lattice-resolving tip endpoints (70.8 min; 116 min with a disclosed piezo-walker jam). Lower bound reflects apprenticeship runs where the agent first had to request permission and a graduation run that needed two human steering messages. Disclosed gates: mutating tools are denied unless the operator launches with QUAILBOT_ALLOW_MUTATING_TOOLS=1 (a launch-time switch, not per-action approval; confirmed in paper Methods, README and src/tools/mutation-policy.ts); piezo-voltage control was disabled in the workspace for safety; endpoints were verified post hoc by a human STM expert; bent-tip, hidden walker-jam and exhausted-sample cases needed human disclosure, takeover or physical intervention (Table 1). A weaker model (gpt-5.4-mini) failed under the same jam conditions.

autonomy.note: A3-A4 is defensible and kept, but the human role must be disclosed. Observed closure: the Theorem 4.2 session ledger (author-published, ledger.json) has 1 user message and no follow-ups, 18 entries including a rejected step, a superseded entry, a correction, step and full-solution verification, status 'solved'; the paper says Theorem 4.2 was 'proven entirely by Solver Agent'. No autonomous problem selection. Purely in-silico; no physical loop, so A5 does not apply.

scope.note: Multi-step scientific analysis agent: manifest-declared job DAG over six stages (correlator analysis, renormalization, Fourier transform, perturbative matching, extrapolation, review) with LLM-made data-dependent choices and an LLM literature review. Borderline-adversarial point: all numerics are deterministic and the LLM is consulted only at three bounded points, but this matches catalog precedent (LQCDMaster, A3) and is not a plain software component.

autonomy.note: A3 supported, not higher. Paper Fig. 2/Sec. III: LLM used only for the planning dialogue, bounded 'ask' operations inside stages (fit windows, excited states, Fourier ranges, tail models; responses validated before use) and the final Review, which does not alter results. Plan mode ends with explicit user acceptance of the manifest (README); a valid expert-authored manifest runs directly. Authors themselves frame validation as 'execution of expert-specified workflows'. In-silico only; no hypothesis generation, so not A4. The human acceptance gate should be disclosed in notes.

scope.note: Multi-step scientific data work. The Executor decomposes a request, plans, calls MCP tools to evaluate spatial/temporal/redshift association and returns candidate lists, visualizations and a report. autonomy.note: A3 is supported. Observed closure is in-silico only: user-initiated natural-language tasks that the agent decomposes and executes through multiple tool calls to produce association results and reports. Human gates to disclose: every run starts from a human request, and in the paper's real-catalog application the reported associations were 'independently cross-checked through manual execution of the tools'. The evaluation is a tool-use test on simulated injections (50 GWTC-4.0 events, 650 simulated EM events). The claim that it 'correctly completes all association tasks' across LLM backends applies only to that simulated set.

identity.note: arXiv 2603.20253 resolves (abs HTTP 200, API v4 updated 2026-08-17, no withdrawal notice), title and authors match (Yadi Cao ... Rose Yu, UCSD). The paper abstract links github.com/Rose-STL-Lab/SimulCost-Bench, which belongs to the Rose-STL-Lab GitHub organization ('Machine Learning Research Group at University of California, San Diego'), so it is official. The solver submodule Eydcao/simulcost-tools is owned by the first author (GitHub profile name 'Yadi Cao', UCSD postdoc) and is linked as 'Tools' from the official README. Nothing in the baseline matches by name, alias, arXiv ID or repo (the nearest records are the quantum-simulation and chemical-process-simulation agents, which are different systems). No same-name collision found. ICML 2026 is author-stated only (repo description, arXiv comment); I did not check it against the proceedings.

scope.note: This is a benchmark and harness for LLM agents that call physics simulators. In multi-round mode the model proposes a parameter, calls the solver and reads back convergence, RMSE and accumulated cost, for up to 10 trials (§3.3). That counts as evaluating multi-step simulation and tool use. The task is narrow: it tunes one solver parameter at a time, and single-round mode is a one-shot guess with no agent loop. It is still in scope, comparable to PACE-Bench and PhysGym, and it is not an optimization library.

autonomy.note: B is correct: this is a benchmark/harness. All evaluation is computational simulation, with no physical loop.

access.note: REFUTES the 'open-source' label and the note's claim of an 'Apache-2.0 benchmark and toolkit'. The top-level SimulCost-Bench repo is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file plus GitHub API spdx Apache-2.0), and the Rose-STL-Lab Hugging Face dataset is apache-2.0 (API cardData). However, the harness imports its simulators from the costsci_tools submodule (for example 'from costsci_tools.wrappers.burgers_1d import run_sim_burgers_1d ...'). That submodule is Eydcao/simulcost-tools ('Contains 12 physics-based PDE solvers with cost tracking'). It has no LICENSE file, the GitHub licence API returns 404, and its README and pyproject.toml give no licence. Its nested submodules Eydcao/fem_transient_utils and Eydcao/CSMPM_BOW are also unlicensed, and the bundled EPOCH is GPL-3.0. The paper calls this solver library the 'extensible toolkit', and the benchmark cannot run without it. Following the EarthVerse and LabBench precedent, the honest label is source-available with access_evidence. Relabel to open-source once the solver library carries an OSI licence.

category.note: benchmark matches catalog precedent for agent benchmarks, which all use category benchmark with autonomy B. Other physics-simulation benchmarks such as PACE-Bench and PhysGym are filed under benchmark too, not physics.

urls.note: These URLs returned 200 when fetched: the arXiv abs page, arXiv HTML and arXiv API; the GitHub repo page and LICENSE page; the Hugging Face dataset page and API; the Eydcao/simulcost-tools repo page; and the GitHub API endpoints. Each URL supports its label. The proposed links are fine. I recommend also linking the author-owned solver library so readers can see the licence gap.

text.note: Three corrections are needed. (a) 'Apache-2.0 benchmark and toolkit' is inaccurate because the solver toolkit is unlicensed. (b) inputs: 'cost budgets' is loose. The paper specifies a task, tuning mode and accuracy requirement, and the multi-round budget is up to 10 trials. (c) outputs omit the Bayesian-optimization baseline (§3.5). The paper benchmarks 12 simulators: 11 with analytical cost carry the main results and EPOCH is timed by wall clock and reported separately. The record should say this. The CGYRO statement matches the arXiv v4 comment ('removed CGYRO due to bug in cases search. Will add back soon'). The paraphrase 'pending a bug fix' is acceptable, but the corrected record quotes the comment more closely. The success-rate and cost figures were not restated, so they have no inflation risk.

decisions.name: Avatar: Toward Autonomous End-to-End Orchestration of Scientific Workflows using LLMs
decisions.rationale: Scope resolved on today's full-text read (v1 remains the only version). Avatar is a reference architecture for scientific workflow management systems: orchestrator, executor and provenance actors on the Academy framework, with rule-based or LLM policies (gpt-oss-20b via the ALCF Sophia endpoint). The LLM decides execution control: retries, elastic scaling and campaign-steering actions. Evaluation uses synthetic matrix-multiplication workloads for resilience and scaling, plus an unmodified Colmena active-learning campaign whose property calculation is replaced by a QM9 lookup. Headline gains are compute-waste and GPU-time reductions, not scientific findings. This places Avatar with workflow infrastructure (MAINTENANCE.md excludes 'scientific software components'). Unlike the catalogued HEPTAPOD or ChemOS 2.0 entries, it does not run a domain-science workflow end to end. The E3 steering is the closest it comes to scientific decision-making, and it runs against a lookup oracle. Interpretive scope call; if Michaela prefers to keep workflow-orchestration research as leads, KEEP_HOLD is the alternative, because no code is released either way: the paper has no repository link, and the globus-labs, academy-agents and Parsl org listings and GitHub searches found none.
decisions.reconsider_when: Only if a later version or official release shows Avatar making scientific decisions on a real domain workload (experiment selection judged by scientific outcome, not compute efficiency), with author-released, licensed code.

decisions.rationale: The September blocker is resolved. The paper-linked repository OTeam-AI4S/ADMET-EvO, which returned 404 on 2026-09-11, now returns 200. It is public, not a fork, and carries an MIT LICENSE recognised by the GitHub licence API. It contains the agent package (admet_agent/ with brain.py, openai_brain.py, policy_brains.py and cli.py), tests, a CHANGELOG (0.3.0, 2026-09-07) and the paper's supplementary tox43 task tables. Repo creation date (2026-08-20) and last push (2026-09-07) predate the September check, so it was probably private then; this is inference, not verified. The paper front matter links this org repo; its only listed contributor is YilinWang33 (Yilin Wang, equal-contribution author and README contact). An earlier personal repo YilinWang33/ADMET-EvO (MIT, created 2026-08-11) exists, but the paper link is used. Scope fits: a hypothesis-driven computational research loop (endpoint formalisation, falsifiable hypotheses, data/feature/model interventions, evidence verdicts, task-space expansion), comparable to AutoProteinEngine. Category biology: arXiv primary q-bio.QM, and the endpoints are pharmacokinetic/toxicological, including zebrafish and cellular assays; chemistry is defensible by LIDDIA/MADD precedent. Autonomy A3-A4: the paper describes an autonomous LLM-policy loop that expanded to 43 toxicity tasks. The released runtime defaults to a rule-based planner (LLM optional), and external data need recorded scientific review before admission. Closure is computational only. Not checked: execution of the code, reproduction of the 96.77 score, and which LLM the paper used (my search for common model names found none).

scope.note: This is a multi-step computational research loop: endpoint contract, then a hypothesis plus one registered action on the data/feature/model axis, then a deterministic evaluator, an evidence verdict and a state update with retain/rollback/stop. It also selects and formalizes new toxicity tasks. That is more than a one-shot predictor, comparable to the catalogued AutoProteinEngine (A3). Caveat from the repo's own claim boundary (docs/release_status_2026-08-23.md): it 'does not claim that the current research policy is predictively superior to expanded AutoML'. Scope still holds, because the catalog records research-workflow agents regardless of whether they beat AutoML.

autonomy.note: A3-A4 is defensible and should stay a range. The paper's Sec. 3.1 describes a closed loop in which the LM proposes hypotheses and actions while a deterministic evaluator and update operator judge the results, and Sec. 2.5 claims the system autonomously selected and formalized 43 tasks outside its initial knowledge base. Factors that cap it below a clean A4: (a) actions are restricted to registered, schema-validated actions, and the planner cannot execute arbitrary code (docs/gpt56_integration.md); (b) the released runtime defaults to the rule planner, with the LLM optional; (c) the repo's own claim boundary calls it a 'bounded, auditable ADMET research workflow'; (d) the paper does not name the LLM or report how many cycles were LLM-driven versus rule-driven. Repo docs configure an OpenAI-compatible model ('gpt-5.6-sol'); that model name is a repo configuration string and was not checked against any vendor source. Human gate: external data become training data only after recorded scientific review. All closure is computational: no lab, wet or experimental-validation text was found in the paper body, and the zebrafish/cellular endpoints are existing ToxCast assay labels, not new experiments. A5 is not applicable.

decisions.name: SolutionsX: supergravity theories/solutions as code, with an agentic workflow for machine-verifiable physics
decisions.rationale: September held this for a clearer agentic-workflow release and a scope ruling. Both resolved today. The agent toolkit is not a paper claim any more: agent/ is published inside the official repository (waskou/SolutionsX, author Vasil Dimitrov, INRNE Bulgarian Academy of Sciences, matching the paper's single author and the Wolfram Paclet Repository publisher ID), it is covered by a confirmed AGPL-3.0-or-later LICENSE with the bundled corpora under CC BY 4.0, and tagged releases v2.0.0 (2026-08-24) and v2.1.0 (2026-09-02) exist. The toolkit is a genuine agent harness (persistent-kernel driver with time budgets and restart/replay recovery, a cold-kernel reporter that re-runs a script in isolation, symptom-keyed METHODS/TRAPS hint files, a stall ladder that forces the agent to stop and write a report, a separate agent alias so the agent cannot write under the human's identity), and the paper documents three blind runs in which a coding agent given only the repository, the toolkit and a task codified a published supergravity solution correctly in under three hours; the five agent-authored entries are published under Data/Vasko-bot/ so the claim is checkable. Scope ruling: the Mathematica/xAct package alone would be a scientific software component, but the published artifact is a tool environment plus a demonstrated agentic workflow, which is the same basis on which the catalog keeps ToolUniverse, ChemMCP, PUDA and AEcroscopyWave, so I include it with an explicit component boundary in the notes. Autonomy A2-A3 on observed closure: the agent runs multi-step shell/kernel work with its own verification and stop criteria, but the external coding agent is not identified in the paper, the kit is marked experimental, and the human runs the produced notebook; nothing supports A4. No name collision: no existing record or alias contains SolutionsX.

decisions.name: Human-agent discovery of reconfigurable in-plane ferroelectric superdomain control
decisions.rationale: September could only read the abstract (arXiv HTML was 404, still 404 today) and held the physical-loop, human-gate and artifact appraisal. I read the full PDF (28 pages, HTTP 200) and the author repository, so all three are now resolved. Physical closure is demonstrated, not claimed: in the agent-controlled Campaign 2 the agent issued instrument commands to a real piezoresponse microscope through a Python wrapper, closed nine propose-preflight-write-read-analyze-decide cycles, self-halted eight of them without operator intervention, rejected two of its own provisional rules by direct measurement, and the campaign ended with the letters UTK written into the in-plane superdomain orientation of a PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3(111) film. That is A5 under the catalog definition (real laboratory loop), with the human gates disclosed: the operator set the target and kept stop authority, an exclusive instrument lock plus scanner-range, bias, footprint and write-budget limits bounded candidate writes, and the authors report that the function meant to apply all 29 preflight checks was not called on the normal driver path. The reusable artifact exists and is licensed: the repository named in the paper's data-availability statement (github.com/RichardLiuCoding/Publications/tree/main/SPARC-PZTO111) carries MIT for code and CC BY 4.0 for the memory files, records and derived data, and its CITATION.cff lists the same six authors with first-author and Kalinin institutional e-mails, which makes it author-endorsed. Limits recorded in the notes: raw frames are deposited separately with no DOI yet, acquisition scripts are machine-specific and published as a record of what ran, and the physics rests on few areas of one film. Categorised physics per catalog precedent for materials-physics microscopy agents (AEcroscopyWave); named with the expansion of the acronym because SPARC is a heavily reused abbreviation elsewhere, and no existing record or alias uses it.

decisions.name: AutoKD: Autonomous Knowledge Discovery
decisions.rationale: The specific unresolved condition was a licensed release. Checked today: the author-endorsed repository named in the abstract (github.com/GeQinwen/AutoKD) is still public and still carries no licence. The GitHub licence endpoint returns 404, the repository metadata field license is null, there is no LICENSE file in the root listing, no releases and no tags, and the last push is 2026-05-07, four months before the preprint and unchanged since the September pass; setup.py declares no licence classifier and the README ends with a datasets table, no licence line. So the repository is at most source-available, not open-source, and nothing changed. Two further reasons to keep it on hold rather than add it as source-available: the paper's demonstrated closure is cumulative hypothesis generation and statistical testing on three tabular corpora (World Values Survey Wave 7, Amazon Books reviews, SciSciNet v2), which are survey, consumer-review and scientometric tables, so the natural-science scope the catalog requires is not established by the demonstration; and the evaluation is quality judgement against published findings, not an independent validation harness. I did not find another author-endorsed release: a GitHub repository search for AutoKD returned only unrelated projects (KDE wallet scripts, keyboard firmware, a banana-wilt classifier) and a search for the system's distinctive insight-graph phrasing returned nothing. This is my search, not proof of absence.

If the licence appears but the only demonstrations remain survey, consumer-review and scientometrics tables, judge natural-science scope explicitly before adding, and prefer source-available with access_evidence if the licence is restrictive.

decisions.name: Agentic BAIM-LLM Evaluation (ABLE): Benchmarking LLM Use of Protein Design Tools
decisions.rationale: The September condition (licensed runtime or benchmark release) is unachievable by the authors' explicit design, so carrying it as an open hold would be a hold that can never resolve. The paper states that the full prompts and the ABLE0 rubric are deliberately not shared and that the target pathogen, the modified properties and the scoring mechanism are redacted for dual-use reasons; SecureBio's GitHub organisation (27 repositories listed today) contains no ABLE, BAIM or protein-design benchmark repository, and the cited Inspect AI repository is the UK AI Security Institute's framework, not an author artifact. I therefore apply the catalog's paper-only route, with the direct precedent of asa-abc-bench, an unreleased ICML 2026 agentic-biosecurity benchmark catalogued paper-only in June. The significance test is met on documented use rather than on a release: an institutional biosecurity evaluator ran nine tasks (ABLE0 planning plus ABLE1-8 execution covering PDB structure retrieval, ProteinMPNN sequence generation and AlphaFold3-output validation) against 15 frontier models with 10 repetitions per task, measured that seven named closed-weight models refused every task, and compared a subset with a timed human expert baseline; the work was presented at the NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on Biosecurity Safeguards for Generative AI, per the arXiv comment field. Autonomy B as a benchmark. No existing record or alias in the catalog is named ABLE, so there is no collision, but the acronym is generic and the aliases carry the full expansion. The honest limits (deliberate redaction, no runnable release, proxy workflow, not wet-lab validated) belong in the notes, and I flag for the lane reviewer that a stricter reading of 'prefer HOLD over padding' would keep this on hold instead.

decisions.rationale: September held FUSION on scope (new skill-pack admission), not on artifacts; licence and release were already in place then (v0.1.0 published 2026-08-11, MIT) and nothing about them has changed except continued maintenance (last push 2026-10-02). Full-text review resolves the scope question in favour of admission. FUSION ships a runnable agent (unsigned binaries for macOS/Linux on the v0.1.0 release, an opencode fork) together with the skills and an offline literature layer, so it meets the criterion September itself applied to VALG (a released reusable agent runtime, not only procedural assets). The paper documents an end-to-end computational workflow from a one-sentence request: build, verified-input deck, convergence study, independent second-solver check, EXFOR retrieval, reporting that no data exist at the requested energy, and comparison at measured energies. That matches the August physics precedent of skill-delivered agents admitted at A3 (SMEFT pheno agent, NNStar, LQCDMaster) rather than generic skill libraries (K-Dense, retained only as selected infrastructure). Autonomy A3: computational closure only, and the paper states that physical judgment stays with the user. ROOT FLAG: this reverses a September root-level scope hold without new artifact evidence. If root keeps the moratorium on new skill-delivered systems, downgrade to KEEP_HOLD and apply the same rule to IOBRpy, VALG and SolutionsX. No same-name collision found in the identity baseline (0 rows matching 'fusion').
decisions.reconsider_when: Root rules that domain skill packs shipped with a rebranded general coding agent are in scope (apply the same ruling to VALG, IOBRpy and SolutionsX in this cycle; if VALG, a Codex-only skill bundle, is promoted, FUSION should be promoted for consistency), or FUSION releases FUSION-specific agent logic beyond branding (a controller or workflow layer), or documented independent use appears.

scope.note: Contested, root decision. For admission: the paper documents one recorded multi-step computational session (deck from verified example, convergence study, second-solver check with COLOSS, EXFOR retrieval, reporting that no 50 MeV data exist, recomputation at measured energies); August admitted skill-delivered physics agents (SMEFT-Pheno-Agent, NNStar, LQCDMaster). Against: September held FUSION specifically as a 'new skill-pack' and explicitly said retaining K-Dense/ToolUniverse-type infrastructure is not blanket admission. September's FUSION evidence was the arXiv abs+HTML only, but the repository now fetched confirms that characterization: README 'The skills are the project. The bundled CLI is one way to run them, not the point'; 'fusion is a rebranded opencode and everything here works under a stock opencode install too'; paper: engine is 'a brand-only patch'. The skills directory has 26 entries (azure2 ... vhlle, exfor-data, kb-search, literature-wiki, research-profile, fusion-setup, sfresco) and no controller or workflow skill; AGENTS.md only gives verification discipline and onboarding. Unlike SMEFT-Pheno-Agent (12-phase workflow) or NNStar (whole inference workflow in one skill), each FUSION code skill wraps one tool (install/run/parse/benchmark); end-to-end behaviour comes from the generic agent composing them. The proposal's new argument (a runnable agent ships, meeting the VALG criterion) was already true in September (release 2026-08-11) and the runnable part is not FUSION-specific. Commits since 2026-09-11 are corpus/EXFOR/language maintenance only.

decisions.name: QMClaw: A Scalable General-purpose Framework for Quantum Measurement and Control
decisions.rationale: Material change: an MIT-licensed repository QMC-AI/QMClaw exists (created 2026-08-27, so September missed it rather than it being new). Its README tells users to 'cite our paper' and links arXiv 2609.04674, and commit author names zzzq_fan and Lvping-1024 resemble paper authors Zhiqiang Fan and Ping Lv. Still unresolved: (1) ownership. The paper v1 (only version) contains no repository link; QMC-AI is an anonymous personal account created the same day as the repo; the README still carries template placeholders (YOUR_USERNAME/qmclaw-skills); the LICENSE copyright is 'QMClaw Contributors'; three vendor submodules come from a third contributor's (Secsix) repositories and their licences were not checked. Name-matching is suggestive, not explicit author endorsement. (2) Physical closure. Sec. 3.1 reports one natural-language-driven single-qubit tune-up on real superconducting hardware 'without manual intervention', but the abstract describes validation 'using real quantum device dataset'. The quantitative results replay a historical session (session_20251104, 73 qubits, 2476 steps), and the limitations name limited sessions and a single device type. One qualitative run is weaker than catalogued A5 quantum precedents (Vibe Calibration, k-agents). (3) Shape. The repository presents itself as 'QMClaw Skills' (agent skill bundle plus server/web front end), which touches the same skill-delivered scope question flagged on FUSION. The hardware loop requires the authors' LabRAD-controlled instruments, so practical access would be lab-gated even with MIT code.
decisions.reconsider_when: Promote as physics/open-source once a paper version, institutional page or the authors explicitly link QMC-AI/QMClaw (ownership). Autonomy depends on what the record shows. A3 with the hardware loop disclosed as lab-gated if only the single qualitative run stands. A5 range only if repeated or quantified real-hardware calibration runs are reported (compare Vibe Calibration, k-agents). Resolve the skill-delivered scope rule together with FUSION. Re-check vendor submodule licences (Secsix/Quantum-Calibration-Agent-Blueprint, hermes-agent, QubitClient) before labelling open-source.

decisions.name: A computable representation of the physical laboratory enables verifiable workflows
decisions.rationale: September could not read the full text (HTML 404); arXiv HTML is still 404, so today's review used the arXiv PDF (200, 52 pages incl. Supplementary Information). The scope question is now resolved. The contribution is a formal laboratory representation (typed research objects, capability-bound operations, a five-operator workflow algebra) with Function-Skill conversion, workflow generation, static analysis and stateful-simulation checks before dispatch. That makes it laboratory-representation and verification infrastructure, a scientific software component, not a system shown performing multi-step scientific work. The Methods state that no workflow was physically executed and no wet-lab outcome comparison was made. Artifacts are not public either: code and the Function-Skill library are 'Additional Files' with no version tag or commit, and the authors say the internal release page is not a public repository. The group (USTC with Huawei co-authors; Linjiang Chen, Jun Jiang) is the same as the catalogued ChemAgents (A5, lab-gated) and LabBench (B). A later paper that uses this layer inside a demonstrated physical loop should be reviewed as that system or as an update to those records, not as this paper. No public repository for this paper appeared in the pic-ai-robotic-chemistry organisation listing (newest repo 2026-09-20, 'mlipipe'); that is a search result, not proof of absence.
decisions.reconsider_when: Not as this paper. Review afresh only if the authors release a public, licensed system that uses this representation inside an agent loop with demonstrated physical execution; if so, check first whether it is an update to ChemAgents or LabBench rather than a new identity.

The author-endorsed repository LQgdwind/SciLENS (linked in the abstract) still has no LICENSE file: the GitHub licence API returns 404, the blob URL returns 404, the 61-entry recursive tree contains no licence or COPYING file, and the README has no licence statement. decisions.name: HyGRAIL: Cost-Aware and Evidence-Grounded Scientific Hypothesis Discovery over Knowledge Graphs
decisions.rationale: Scope resolved against the catalog boundary. HyGRAIL (UIUC) is a knowledge-graph link-prediction method: a GNN scores typed candidate links, ambiguous ones are routed to a single LLM review call over retrieved graph evidence, and the output is an accept/reject decision scored by closed-world link-prediction F1 on MatKG. There is no planning, tool execution, experiment, analysis or reporting loop, so it is a scientific ML component rather than a system performing multi-step scientific work. Release status is also unchanged: arXiv is still v1 (2026-09-02) with no code link, and GitHub searches found no repository (search result, not proof of absence).
decisions.reconsider_when: A later version turns HyGRAIL into an iterative agent that generates, tests and revises hypotheses with tools, data analysis or experiments (not only link classification) and the authors release licensed code.

scope.note: Borderline, but within the letter of MAINTENANCE.md. The released pipeline runs four smolagents CodeAgents in sequence: (1) build tissue networks from ProteomicsDB iBAQ data, with an agent-chosen filter and threshold plus a rebuild-if-unsatisfying loop; (2) build consensus networks, run Leiden clustering and filter housekeeping genes; (3) annotate from HPA, hu.MAP 3.0, g:Profiler and STRING; (4) write per-pair reports with MyGene.info, Open Targets and Europe PMC novelty counts plus web search. That is multi-step scientific work (code/tool execution, analysis, literature checks, hypothesis reporting). None of the exclusions applies: it is not a base model, not a component or library, and not a one-off case-study audit. The ALD rejection was an LLM evaluation with no reusable agent; here the agent code is released and runnable. Weaknesses that argue for HOLD under 'prefer HOLD over padding with obscure entries': (a) the system has no name and is study-specific, with ProteomicsDB tissue groups hard-coded; (b) the repo is a Colab working notebook (hard-coded Drive path in cell 0, 4 commits on one day, no releases, 0 stars); (c) the paper is a biology application paper and does not evaluate the agents against a baseline or a manual analysis; (d) the agents mostly call author-written @tool functions in a prescribed order. The September decision recorded scope as screened and held only on the artifact/licence gate, which is now met. Precedent for small licensed workflow agents: Orchestra (regulatory discovery), A3; Omics Data Discovery Agents, A2. Net: admissible, provided the notes disclose these limits.

autonomy.note: A2-A3 is supported; A4/A5 are not. Observed closure: inside stage 1 the agent picks filtering parameters and may rebuild the network when it judges quality poor (notebook prompt step 5; paper section 4.1.3, 'iteratively adjusts τ'). Stages 2-4 follow fixed step lists per tissue pair. Humans run the stages cell by cell and select items through hand-edited filters (e.g. 'if ind < 56', 'if not (brain and adrenal)', 'if ind < 328'). The headline landscape statistics (binomial test, degree-preserving permutation test, BH correction, heatmaps) are plain author-written Python in notebook cells 21-29, not agent actions. Appendix 5 says the case-study narratives were written by the authors from the agent reports and enrichment tables. Everything is computational, with no physical loop. The notebook ships with all cell outputs cleared, so the agent runs can be observed only through the paper and the Drive results snapshot (reachable; contents not inspected). A2 alone would also be defensible.

decisions.name: Agentic AI for operating scientific instruments for nanoscale characterization
decisions.rationale: September hold was conditional on a full-text check of physical closure and identity; arXiv HTML is still 404, so the v1 PDF (47 pp.) was read in full. Physical closure is demonstrated on real hardware: AFM Pilot iteratively reads live height/error data, judges artifacts and executes bounded setpoint/gain/scan-rate changes on a custom open-hardware AFM (calibration grating, butterfly wing, KPFM), and five matched sessions from identical detuned starts showed no significant difference from human operators (Wilcoxon, n=5). Identity: EPFL LBNI (Fantner group) system, distinct from AILA (Mandal et al., cited by the authors as prior work), ORNL AEcroscopyWave, TEM Agent and CALMS; no name/alias collision in asa_identity.tsv. Access remains paper-only: the paper promises agent code, benchmark data and evaluation scripts 'upon publication' at Open-SPM/Agentic_AFM, which returns 404 (web and GitHub API); even the RePySPM controller repository the paper calls available returns 404 at Open-SPM/RePySPM. Promoted as paper-only under the significant-system exception because physical instrument closure is demonstrated and measured against experts (same basis as PACE-SIMS, August 2026). Autonomy A3-A5 (TEM Agent precedent): the physical loop is real but limited to imaging-parameter tuning within predefined bounds; humans set experimental intent and resolve ambiguous commands, and the authors explicitly disclaim a self-driving lab. Curator may prefer A5 (CALMS precedent) or KEEP_HOLD until the promised code appears; both are defensible.
decisions.reconsider_when: Access upgrade only: when github.com/Open-SPM/Agentic_AFM (or another EPFL LBNI-endorsed location) becomes public, re-check licence and change access to open-source or source-available and add repo_links; recheck autonomy if a journal version changes the closure claims.

scope.note: Multi-step instrument operation: natural-language command translation with ambiguity checking, iterative acquire-assess-adjust tuning on live hardware with an autonomous stop decision, and post-processing with re-inspection. It does not choose experiments, but the catalog already holds instrument-operation agents (TEM Agent, AEcroscopyWave, CALMS, PACE-SIMS, vibe-calibration), so it is in scope by precedent.

autonomy.note: A3-A5 is supported. Physical closure is observed: AFM Pilot retrieves live height/error data, scores artifacts by AI vision, and 'executes the proposed parameter updates through AFM Messenger' (p.4); Supplementary S3 (p.40-42) shows a 10-iteration hardware session with autonomous parameter changes and a STOP decision. Lower bound A3 fits Messenger (operator-clarified commands) and Doctor (pre-approved tools). Same range as the TEM Agent precedent; A5 alone (CALMS, vibe-calibration) is also defensible but the narrow action space (bounded setpoint/integral gain/scan rate) argues for the range. Gates that MAINTENANCE.md requires to be disclosed are only partly in the proposed notes: approach and scan initiation need operator confirmation (p.20), tuning runs inside operator-defined bounds (p.21), and in S4 the operator overrode an AI ringing mis-score (p.46). Corrected notes add these.

decisions.name: The Little Scientist: LLM Agent-Driven Discovery via the Scientific Method
decisions.rationale: Today I checked each part of the September condition, scope, licence and dependence on upstream infrastructure, against primary sources. (1) Licence: both author repositories, which the arXiv comment field links, carry Apache-2.0 LICENSE files (GitHub licence API spdx Apache-2.0; LICENSE text fetched). (2) Scope: little-scientist-delta-v contains the framework itself: Scientist and Kuhn agent prompts and workspaces, the watcher, the Scientist-to-Kuhn handoff and Kuhn selector, the validator and evaluation harness, setup scripts, OpenClaw setup docs and an architecture document. The DALE README names delta-v as the framework repository. One discrepancy: the paper's Code availability points the framework to little-scientist-dale, whose sef/ folder holds only the agent prompt and best strategy. (3) Upstream dependence: the framework needs the external OpenClaw platform for LLM invocation, scheduling and sandboxing, and used GLM-4.7. Autonomy is A3-A4. Agent invocations ran by cron without intervention and the loop includes explicit hypotheses, but the human designed the evaluator and injected the data behind the biggest ProteinGym jump, and the paper describes an optionally human-guided outer loop. Limits recorded in notes: single author; the ProteinGym #1 claim rests on an unmerged pull request (#117, state open, merged false); the framework is packaged per problem and is not a general library. The repositories have not changed since 2026-08-14, so this promotion reflects deeper verification today, not a new release. No name collision in the catalog baseline.

decisions.name: VALG: An Agentic System for ML Theory Research
decisions.rationale: September's open question (reusable runtime or procedural assets) is now answered from the repository tree and docs. The release is a complete MIT-licensed bundle of 17 Codex skills: a controller skill (ml-theory-research-agent), stage skills for literature survey, perspective selection, idea formalization, proof sketch, proof steps, specialized reviews and assembly, plus templates and archived case-study artifacts. There is no standalone program, and it runs inside Codex with subagents. The skills are the research method itself, not wrappers around an existing tool, so this matches admitted precedent: Get Physics Done (a workflow installed into Claude Code/Codex), NNStar (a skill delivered into an agent platform) and Andy (an MIT maths proof-graph system, filed as physics). The authors endorse the repository in the arXiv abstract and in the v2 full text. The LICENSE is MIT (GitHub API and raw file). Third-party notices exclude the copied COLT source PDFs and some LaTeX support files. The repository has had no commits since 2026-08-15 and no releases. Category physics follows the catalog's maths precedent. Autonomy is A3-A4: autopilot carries a run from research direction to reviewed theorem candidates, but interactive mode puts a human-expert checkpoint after each pre-proof stage, and the paper's candidates were only roughly audited by humans.

scope.note: Multi-step theory-research workflow: literature survey -> perspective selection -> idea generation -> formalization into a fixed theorem contract -> proof-dependency graph -> global diagnostic -> step proofs -> assembly -> four specialized reviews plus aggregate verdict, with failure-localized repair routing. It is neither a base model nor a prover library. September's open question (reusable runtime vs procedural assets) is answered: README says 'The skills/ directory is the reusable product', and the paper itself labels tree/main/skills as VALG. Precedents: GPD (workflow installed into Claude Code/Codex) and NNStar (skill in an agent platform).

autonomy.note: A3-A4 holds, but the human role in the published runs is larger than the proposal's rationale implies. The rationale says autopilot 'carries a run from research direction to reviewed theorem candidates', but no archived run shows that end to end. Worker logs: 8 of 9 runs record run_mode=interactive and/or checkpoint actions (approved, re-search, re-generate) in Workflow 1. The 05-dp-pac/sp-02 RUN_CONFIG says 'Run mode: interactive', and its theory_tracker notes fallbacks 'disallowed by checkpoint feedback'. 02-deep-vs-linear/sp-01 records no mode. Both full-progress runs (Online OQ2 = 03/sp-02; One-bit OP1 = 04/sp-01) ran interactive. Observed in-silico closure supporting the A4 upper bound: in ALS OP2 (01/sp-01), after an interactive start, the run switched to RUN_MODE=autopilot on 2026-07-19. It then generated idea_6 and idea_7 from failed sketch reviews (retry_mode=new_idea), formalized them, and proved and reviewed idea_7 to aggregate ACCEPTED (score 8) on 2026-07-21. Workflow 2 (proof, review, repair) runs without human gates in all runs. Purely computational, so A5 is not applicable. The human gate is disclosed in the paper (Sec. 3.1), and the notes should say it was exercised.

decisions.name: Periodic Labs
decisions.rationale: periodic.com now links three first-party technical posts dated 2026-09-15 that the September review could not see. They describe a concrete system: Periodic Neon, an open-weight 1T-parameter model (Kimi K2.6) post-trained by midtraining and RL on Periodic's lab data. It runs in an in-house scientific harness with laboratory context, in-house structure and simulation databases and XRD analysis software. The posts report it deployed in Periodic's labs to analyse powder-XRD results, with evaluation numbers on 134 internal FrontierXRD samples and 198 held-out-chemical-system measurements. That meets the restoration test of a concrete system plus an observed autonomy level, but only for multi-step, tool-using analysis (A2-A3). The same posts describe AI direction of campaigns, synthesis and experiment choice as work being extended. One sentence says AI systems are used for designing, running and learning from experiments, but the posts give no demonstration of it. A5 therefore stays unsupported and must not be restored. Access is lab-gated: internal deployment, with no public API, weights or benchmark release found. Evidence is company-published only (no paper), and the success metric is an LLM-judge ensemble calibrated against expert ratings. Restore the reserved id asa-periodic-labs, renamed to the evidenced system with the company name kept as alias. Category changes from crossdomain to chemistry under the materials-synthesis rule. If root judges a single analysis agent from company posts too thin for a row, the fallback is KEEP_HOLD; I do not recommend that, because the restoration condition is literally met and Bunsen and Claude Science are company-page precedents.
decisions.reconsider_when: Re-check autonomy, and possibly the A5 label, only when first-party evidence shows AI-directed synthesis/experiment selection actually executed in Periodic's labs with outcomes, ideally in a paper or technical report. Re-check access if Neon, the harness or FrontierXRD is released or offered as a service.

scope.note: In scope as a single-task analysis agent. The model works inside a harness that has databases and XRD software, and it executes model-written code in sandboxes (pbox). The infrastructure post shows a typical XRD reasoning trace lasting over an hour, with tool calls. This is a deployed agentic system, so the Intern-S2-Preview 'base-model family' rejection precedent does not apply. Borderline: it covers only one stage (analysis) of Periodic's hypothesize-synthesize-characterize loop.

autonomy.note: A2-A3 is supported. A2: tool use through the harness, shown in the posts. A3: multi-step, multi-hypothesis analysis traces. Nothing beyond analysis is demonstrated. Two present-tense sentences claim more: 'we leverage AI ... to decide what to do next' (Building Labs post) and 'using our AI systems for designing, running, and learning from experiments' (Research post). Neither comes with a demonstration or outcomes, and the announcement post frames campaign direction, synthesis and experiment choice as being extended. A5 stays unsupported, as the proposal says. Self-reported evaluation: internal 134-sample FrontierXRD, scored by an LLM-judge ensemble (judge-expert agreement 74.6% vs expert-expert 77.2%). Consistency flag for root, outside this review: the catalog row asa-lila-sciences shows platform/A5 backed only by a press-release paper link. That looks like the same evidence gap that triggered the Periodic hold. I did not fetch that source.

No public release found: GitHub org periodic-oss has 0 public repos; Hugging Face API searches (periodic-neon, author periodiclabs/periodic-labs, dataset frontierxrd) returned []; gh repo searches for 'periodic neon' and 'FrontierXRD' returned []. Alternative reading: under the README definition, paper-only ('no currently runnable public implementation') would also fit. Either is honest; lab-gated is kept.

decisions.name: IOBRpy
decisions.rationale: Nothing changed since August. The repository was last pushed on 2026-08-03 (commit 'Update documentation'), with no commits since 2026-09-01 and no releases. The bioRxiv preprint is still v1 (2026-07-22) and unpublished. The MIT licence is still confirmed. The README still describes a command-line bulk RNA-seq TME toolkit. Its agent layer (agent-harness/: CLI wrapper, MCP server, Claude Code/Codex commands, plugins and skills) installs integrations so that external coding agents can drive the existing pipeline. IOBRpy has no planner or runtime of its own. The September scope adjudication (component admission unresolved) is a governance decision this lane should not overturn. Tension for root: ClinAgent (a skill/MCP layer for coding agents) and NNStar (a skill installed into an agent platform) are admitted, so a single explicit rule for pipeline-wrapping agent layers would settle IOBRpy either way.
decisions.reconsider_when: When root sets an explicit rule on agent-integration layers around existing pipelines (precedent tension with ClinAgent and NNStar). Also when IOBRpy ships its own planning runtime that chooses analysis steps, or a new preprint version or journal article evaluates agent-driven end-to-end analysis against a baseline. State on 2026-10-10: repository last pushed 2026-08-03, bioRxiv v1 unpublished.

decisions.name: TCellAlign
decisions.rationale: arXiv is still v2 (2026-08-05). The v2 full text has no external code, data or benchmark link: its outbound links are model cards, funders and tools only. GitHub repository search for 'TCellAlign' on 2026-10-10 returned no repository, and code search found only third-party arXiv digests. On scope, the v2 text is clearer than the August note suggested. TCellAlign is a four-agent workflow (Search, Information Extraction, Mapping and Judge agents) that retrieves papers and CELLxGENE-linked datasets, extracts labels with evidence, maps them to a nomenclature and adjudicates iteratively. That plausibly fits the catalog's literature-extraction and annotation-agent precedent at about A2-A3. The blocking issue is now the missing artifact. As an unreleased paper-only system without physical closure or institutional deployment, it stays HOLD.

Then assess it as an A2-A3 literature-and-dataset label-harmonisation agent under the Eunomia, CellTypeAgent and MetaDataGenAgent precedent, and disclose that expert curation built the benchmark. On 2026-10-10 no official repository was found; this is not a claim that none exists.

decisions.name: Sakana Marlin
decisions.rationale: Third cycle on the same scope question, and the official pages now settle it. The product page and FAQ still define Marlin as a B2B 'Virtual CSO' for strategy, market, competitor, technology-trend and regulatory research; the launch post (now verifiable on sakana.ai, dated 2026-06-15) calls it 'an autonomous research assistant for business'; the 2026-09-16 update adds report-reading and PowerPoint export and lists 'universities and research institutes' only among customer types, with no science-domain run, scientific benchmark or science-facing mode. The release appeared on 2026-09-16/17, after the September review, so the hold condition is now met. scope.note: Multi-step scientific work in a single pipeline: measurement extraction from arXiv/HEPData, an SM prediction template with theory uncertainties via MadGraph, SMEFTatNLO Wilson-coefficient scans and kappa extraction, datacard assembly and validation, and an SFitter global fit, with reviewer agents at each stage. This is not a base model, an optimisation library or a single software component. It is an agent system wrapped around domain tools, the same pattern as the catalog's existing HEPTAPOD and SMEFT-Pheno-Agent records.

autonomy.note: A3 is supported and conservative. The paper states that every step is supervised by a physicist (Sec. 5). It says it deliberately does not build an autonomous MadAgents campaign (Sec. 4) and that every agent run is supervised and driven by a physicist (App. C). The agents chain extraction, re-simulation, the SMEFT scan, datacard and fit, asking the physicist only at high-impact choices (observable, operator set, EFT order). Closure is in-silico (MadGraph/SFitter on a SLURM cluster), so A5 is excluded. Persistent human steering argues against A4. The human gate is disclosed in the notes.

decisions.name: Argonne atomistic framework
decisions.rationale: The August reconsider condition (official repo becomes fetchable) is now met. The paper itself is still unreadable to automated access: the RSC landing page, the doi.org redirect and the OpenAlex OA PDF all returned 403 behind a Cloudflare challenge, which I did not try to bypass. Crossref (200) confirms the paper: 'Multi-agentic AI framework for end-to-end atomistic simulations', Vriza, Kornu, Koneru, Chan and Sankaranarayanan (Argonne CNM/ALCF and UIC), Digital Discovery 5:440-452 (2026), VOR licence CC BY 3.0, no update-to/retraction relation. A GitHub code search for the paper title turned up ANL-NST/LAMMPS-Agents. Its README title and tagline match the Crossref title and abstract word for word. The MIT LICENSE is copyrighted to 'Polybot Self-Driving Lab', Argonne's self-driving-lab group. GitHub lists katerinavr as the only contributor (commits from 2025-06-23 to 2025-11-03), and that profile reads 'Katerina Vriza' at 'Argonne National Laboratory'. The same org also hosts the CASTING nanocluster-optimisation code. I treat this as the official, first-author repository. I could not check whether the article's code-availability statement links to it, because the publisher returned 403. The software is AutoGen-based: a group chat of admin, structure, potential, LAMMPS input-creator, elastic, reviewer, HPC, analysis/vision, web-surfer and phonopy agents, with up to 800 rounds. Runs go to a local LAMMPS or through an HPC-manager module. The public code sets the input-creator agent to human_input_mode='ALWAYS' and ships a ChromaDB 'teachability' memory built from human teachings. Closure is computational only, with a human gate in the shipped configuration, so I rate it A3. It is in scope (multi-step simulation workflow, not a library). Category is chemistry, following the AtomAgents, DynaMate and MatClaw precedent. I checked for duplicates: asa-chemgraph is a different Argonne team with no shared authors (Crossref, August), and the identity table has no LAMMPS-Agents, ANL-NST or Vriza entry. Limits: GitHub has no tagged release; the README points to a 'results' folder of exemplar runs that is not in the current tree; the last push was 2025-11-03. Post-add follow-up: if the article's text becomes readable, check its code-availability statement and how much human gating the reported runs used, and re-rate if needed.

decisions.name: Edison Finch
decisions.rationale: The August and September checks looked only at the edisonscientific.com product page, which still does not mention Finch (homepage 200, 0 matches). Other first-party sources do. (1) Edison's own client documentation (EdisonScientific/edison-client-docs, Apache-2.0, last push 2026-02-17) maps the hosted Data Analysis job JobNames.ANALYSIS to the alias JobNames.FINCH. (2) The current Edison docs Agents page lists five agents: Kosmos, Literature, Analysis, Precedent and Molecules. Analysis is described for flow cytometry and RNA-seq. (3) The official FutureHouse repository Future-House/finch (formerly data-analysis-crow; that name now redirects) is Apache-2.0. It has releases v1.0.0 (2025-03-04) and v1.5.0 (2025-09-30, 'the release used for the BixBench paper v1.5 results'), and its last push was 2026-04-22. (4) The Robin paper (arXiv 2505.13400, v1, not withdrawn) describes Finch as the data-analysis agent that Robin runs as up to ten independent notebook trajectories on wet-lab data. The BixBench abstract (arXiv 2503.00096) mentions 'a custom agent framework we open source', which matches Finch's README. The lead is therefore substantiated: Finch is a distinct, named, released agent. It is not in the catalog (identity table and agents_final.json contain no Finch, data-analysis-crow or fhda entry). I recommend a standalone open-source row, consistent with the separate rows for Robin, PaperQA3, ether0 and Aviary. Recommended companion amendment, outside this batch's decision: asa-futurehouse-platform-agents-crow-falcon-owl-phoenix lists only Crow, Falcon, Owl and Phoenix. It should mention the hosted Analysis (Finch) agent and the current product names (Literature, Precedent, Molecules) from docs.edisonscientific.com/agents. If the curator prefers no new row, the fallback is MATCH_EXISTING with only that amendment. Autonomy is A3: given data and a question, Finch carries out the multi-step analysis computationally, while experiments and data upload stay with the scientist. Limits: the Finch README still says 'Hosted Agent: Coming soon!' and gives the old install URL. The hosted Analysis agent is documented with extra protein and figure tools, so it may differ from the public code. edison-client 0.17.0 was published on PyPI on 2026-10-09; I did not download it to inspect its current JobNames enum.

decisions.name: MACROS
decisions.rationale: The September hold was for a detailed autonomy and release appraisal. The arXiv HTML is still 404, but the PDF (v1, 16 pages, 200) was read in full. Despite the 'multi-agent' label, MACROS's 'agents' are modality-specific decoder-only transformers (NMR, IR and molecule agents) trained on more than 100M simulated and 1.6M experimental spectra-structure pairs. They are wired into a fixed draft-rethink-refine inference loop: Spec2Mol proposes SMILES, Mol2Spec simulates spectra and ranks candidates, and PromptSpec2Mol refines them. There is no LLM planner, tool selection, code execution or instrument control; the authors contrast it with LLM-based approaches. 'Closed-loop' means test-time refinement of a structure-elucidation model, not experimental closure. The real-world evaluation is a blinded study with three organic spectroscopists, using MACROS as decision support. Under the catalog scope rules this is a specialised scientific model/software component, not a multi-step research agent, so I propose REJECT_SCOPE in place of an indefinite hold. Release status, for the record: the 16-page PDF has no code or data availability statement (no GitHub, Zenodo or Hugging Face link). Methods and Supplementary Notes are referenced but not in the PDF. A GitHub repository search for MACROS returned no matching project. Both are statements about my search, not proof that nothing exists.
decisions.reconsider_when: Only if the authors release (with a licence) an agentic version that plans tool, code or instrument actions, for example MACROS embedded in an automated laboratory loop. A code release of the current model pipeline alone would not change the scope decision.

changes.old: Demonstrated autonomous discovery of lithium halide spinel ionic conductors across 352 synthesis campaigns using a self-driving glovebox robotic laboratory with integrated LLM-based experimental planning.
changes.new: Robotic platform in an N2-filled glovebox for solid-state synthesis of air-sensitive inorganic materials, with LLM agents (abductive abnormality-detection, inductive pattern-finding, and a Bayesian-optimization-assisted variant; GPT-5 by default) designing the experiments. In one campaign of 352 lithium halide spinel samples, the first 77 were designed by researchers, 12 were submitted manually, and 263 were proposed and executed in self-driving mode. Characterization is semi-automated: XRD samples are sealed by hand and measured outside the glovebox, and agent designs pass manually defined feasibility and safety checks before execution. The share of samples with good ionic conductivity and high spinel purity rose from 1.33% in the first 75 agent-proposed samples to 5.33% in the final 75. The code is public but carries no licence text (checked 2026-10-10), so the record is source-available; the campaign dataset is on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0.

decisions.notes: Licence check covered the repo root and all four subdirectories (riskqa_evaluation, tool_curation, mimic_evaluation, ed_evaluation). The recursive tree has one licence file, the root LICENSE; subdirectory READMEs have no licence or copyright wording; there is no pyproject/setup.cfg/package.json (requirements.txt only). LICENSE history: created 2024-10-09 (8bb4bb9) as an NCBI notice, changed to NLM on 2025-03-28 (d44d730); the change only swapped the header. Classification judgement: the text is a public-domain notice, not an OSI-approved licence, but it grants unrestricted use and is a standalone file at the root, so it is none of the source-available triggers (missing text, README-only declaration, NC/custom-restrictive terms). Labelling it source-available would wrongly suggest restrictions, so open-source stays. Residual caveats for the reviewer: (1) public-domain status comes from US copyright law and the notice does not address rights outside the US; (2) the notice says the work was written by US Government employees on official duty, but some co-authors are at non-federal institutions. Neither is a restriction stated in the text. CONSISTENCY: sibling records asa-geneagent (ncbi-nlp/GeneAgent, NLM notice) and asa-genegpt (ncbi/GeneGPT, NCBI notice) were flagged NOASSERTION in the same sweep. I fetched their raw LICENSE headers today and both are the same US Government Work public-domain notice, so they should get the same treatment. Also: access_evidence currently appears only on source-available records; the schema allows it on any record and validate_catalog.py requires it only for source-available, so adding it to an open-source record is valid but new. The GitHub HTML blob URL for LICENSE returned 503 on two attempts (curl and WebFetch), so the raw URL is used as evidence. No lane-proposed problems exist for asa-agentmd in asa_existing_updates.json (19 entries, none with this id). WebSearch not used.

The licence sweep was right that liu-shiqiang/CellAgent has no licence file, but the bigger problem is that this repo is not the paper's code: its owner (Shiqiang Liu, Northeast Forestry University) is not among the 15 authors, the bioRxiv v4 code statement promises GitHub code only after acceptance, and the ICLR 2026 camera-ready names https://github.com/23AIBox/cellagent instead. The paper's 'open-source' wording is a declaration without licence text. Autonomy A3 retained (in-silico analysis agent; consistent with catalog precedent for AutoBA/BioMaster). inputs/outputs kept; outputs could optionally be widened to name batch correction, spatial domain identification and ST imputation, which the paper benchmarks. bioRxiv preprint licence is CC BY-NC-ND (paper text, not code). IDENTITY (needs a decision, not applied): this record duplicates asa-chemagent-self-updating-memory. Both cite the same paper (arXiv 2501.06590) and repo (gersteinlab/chemagent), with identical inputs, outputs, autonomy and notes; both were already present in this form before v2.0.0 (git commit d1cf43b).

There is no other LICENSE/COPYING variant, no pyproject/setup/package.json, and no README licence statement. The code is a U.S. Government Work with no use or reproduction restriction, which is more permissive than MIT, so commercial_use is true. A strict literal reading of 'custom licence -> source-available' would give the opposite answer, so this is a rule to write down, not a fact I can verify. Caveats: (1) the public-domain status is under US copyright law; the paper's rights line notes foreign copyright protection may apply (stated for the article, not the code). (2) The repo also carries third-party gene-set data (GO, MSigDB, NeST subsets) whose own terms are not covered by the NLM notice; not checked. (3) Running the agent needs a proprietary Azure OpenAI GPT-4 key (README). (4) Zenodo deposit v1.1.0 is tagged CC BY 4.0 while GitHub only has tag v1.0.0; minor inconsistency, no access impact. Other checks: both record URLs resolve (GitHub 200, Nature 200 via cookie redirect); repo is the official one named in the paper's Code availability; inputs/outputs/autonomy A2 consistent with README and paper (no physical loop).
