decisions.notes: LICENSING. The only licence text is the root LICENSE, created 2023-05-28 in commit a1b0545, its only commit. It is the standard NCBI 'PUBLIC DOMAIN NOTICE' for a United States Government Work. GitHub's detector maps it to key 'other', which shows up as NOASSERTION. The text is not an OSI-approved licence, but it places no restriction on use or reproduction and sits as a standalone file at the repo root. It therefore meets none of the source-available triggers (missing text, README-only declaration, NC/custom-restrictive terms). Calling it source-available would wrongly suggest restrictions, so access stays open-source and commercial_use is true. The reviewer may want a catalogue-wide rule for US-Government public-domain notices; three ASA records share this pattern: asa-genegpt, asa-agentmd and asa-geneagent. The asa-agentmd agent reported that asa-geneagent's LICENSE (ncbi-nlp/GeneAgent) is the same NLM notice; I did not fetch that file myself. Remaining caveats are not restrictions in the text: (1) public-domain status comes from US copyright law, and the notice does not address rights outside the US; (2) one oddity: the notice's 'Please cite' line names a different NCBI paper ('BioCPT: Contrastive Pre-trained Transformers with Large-scale PubMed Search Logs...'), apparently copied from another NCBI repo. It does not change the terms, and the README's citation block correctly cites GeneGPT. No subdirectory licence exists: the record links the repo root and the tree has no nested LICENSE/COPYING. There is no package metadata (no pyproject/setup.cfg/setup.py/package.json). OTHER CHECKS. Lane-proposed problems: none. asa_existing_updates.json has 19 entries and none has this id or mentions GeneGPT. URLs: the GitHub repo returns 200. The OUP paper URL returns 403 to curl because the publisher blocks bots, but it loaded through WebFetch, and Crossref, PubMed esummary and PMC (200) confirm the same article with no retraction. NOT CHECKED: whether later systems have beaten 0.83 on GeneTuring (hence 'at publication'). The original main.py hard-codes the OpenAI model 'code-davinci-002' (main_turbo.py uses 'gpt-3.5-turbo-16k'); I did not check whether those models are still served, so reproducibility of the exact pipeline is unverified. That is a possible future note, not a record change. WebSearch not used.

decisions.notes: Decision: keep access open-source and add access_evidence; no change to links, autonomy or verified date. Licence: GitHub's NOASSERTION refers to the root LICENSE, which is headed 'Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004' with a 2026 InternAgent Team / Shanghai AI Laboratory copyright line. A word-level diff against https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt shows about a dozen wording changes: 'Work' drops 'whether in Source or Object form'; the 'Contribution' definition lost its head noun ('shall mean, as submitted to the Licensor...'); 'Contributor' drops 'individual or'; s3 'Contribution(s)' -> 'Contributions'; s4(d) drops two qualifiers; s4 last paragraph 'copyright statement to' -> 'license statement for'; s7 'redistributing' -> 'reproducing'; s8 'consequential' -> 'exemplary' and 'any and all' -> 'all'. s2, s5, s6 and s9 are verbatim; no non-commercial, research-only or field-of-use terms anywhere. I read this as a permissive software licence of the Apache type with no added restrictions, so open-source holds under MAINTENANCE.md ('requires a confirmed software licence'), consistent with the ASA precedents where NOASSERTION came from altered or annotated MIT/BSD texts and with today's FM precedent (TomatoPGFM: LICENSE omits standard Apache clauses, adds no restrictions). Contested point for the reviewer: a strict reading of 'custom licence -> source-available' would treat any non-verbatim text as custom. If that reading is preferred, set access source-available and keep this access_evidence with commercial_use true; the licence text grants commercial rights either way. README has no licence statement; no package metadata (pyproject/setup.cfg/package.json) exists for the internagent package; the record links the repo root, so no subdirectory licence applies; subfolder LICENSE files under tasks/ belong to third-party baseline code (MIT, Apache 2.0). History: the repo carried CC BY-NC 4.0 in Aug 2025, had no LICENSE from the 1.0 release (2025-10-13) until the 1.5 release (2026-05-07); the record's verified date (2026-06-16) falls after the current LICENSE appeared. Sibling record asa-internagent-novelseek points to the same repo and has the same NOASSERTION sweep flag; the same finding applies (current HEAD licence covers the repo). Outside the licence question, not changed: (1) autonomy A4-A5: the paper's wet-lab evidence is a passive-voice sfGFP workflow 'coordinated through SCP' reproducing a known result, and the ARG2 wet-lab results appear to be from the original study being reproduced; under the September rule (A5 only for an observed physical loop) the A5 end is thin and a reviewer may prefer A4. (2) 'leads GAIA/HLE/GPQA/FrontierScience' restates the authors' own benchmark claim; 'reports leading results on' would be more precise. URLs: all record URLs resolve (arXiv abs 200, repo 200); the LICENSE blob page returned 503 twice to curl before returning 200, which a later URL audit may also hit transiently. No WebSearch used. asa_existing_updates.json has no lane entry for this id.

decisions.notes: Decision: correct, keeping access 'platform' and autonomy 'A5'. Autonomy adjudication: the preprint and Lila's own blog describe a live physical loop in which the AI proposes compositions, synthesis and electrochemical screening run on instruments (>90% of lab execution automated), results flow back automatically, and the AI ranks the next candidates. MAINTENANCE.md line 11 says human safety gates do not by themselves preclude A5 but must be disclosed; the new notes disclose both human gates (fixture transfers/instrument starts, and candidate review that shrank to a safety check). This matches CRESt (A5, robotic electrocatalyst active-learning loop) and Vibe Calibration (A5 with disclosed human steps). The lane's alternative A4-A5 would understate an observed physical loop; a stricter reader could argue for A4-A5 because humans move samples between every station, so this is an adjudication call and is disclosed in the notes. Caveat: the record is company-level, while the A5 evidence is a single materials campaign; the life-science claims in the press release (antibodies, genetic medicines) remain vendor claims without technical evidence in this record. Licence: root LICENSE is full MIT text and data/LICENSE is CC BY 4.0, both copyright Lila Sciences, confirmed from raw files; README agrees; no pyproject/setup.cfg/package.json exists (requirements.txt only). This licence covers only figure scripts and figure data; it does not change the record's access because the platform code is not public, so no access_evidence object is added (in the current catalog access_evidence appears only on source-available records). The lane's repository description 'MIT' was incomplete and is corrected. github.com blob pages were rate-limited (429/503) intermittently; raw.githubusercontent.com files returned 200 and are cited in the record. Not checked: the full Supporting Information beyond keyword search; whether the press release's other domain claims have technical publications; the origin of the org's 'flyte' repository (not relevant to this record). Only one arXiv PDF was downloaded, for text extraction; no weights or archives.

decisions.notes: Decision no_change: 'open-source' is correct. The repo root LICENSE is full licence text of the LBNL BSD 3-clause variant (SPDX BSD-3-Clause-LBNL, OSI-approved per SPDX License List 3.29.0). It is a software licence, permissive, and allows commercial use. It is not a content licence and not NC/custom-restrictive. GitHub's licensee does not recognise this variant and reports NOASSERTION, which is why the sweep flagged it. The recursive tree has exactly one licence file (root LICENSE). There is no subdirectory licence: api/pyproject.toml uses license = {file = "LICENSE"} with no api/LICENSE beside it (a packaging quirk, not a licensing gap), and web/package.json has no licence field. The README reproduces the same licence text. Every URL in the record resolves today (arXiv 200, GitHub 200). The github.com/.../blob/main/LICENSE HTML view returned a transient 503, so the raw.githubusercontent URL is cited instead. LICENSE = verbatim MIT (Copyright (c) 2024 METR) + an appended NOTE that 'informally request[s]' three contamination precautions (no un-protected solutions published; no feeding material to training APIs; no use to train/improve frontier models except for dangerous-capability evaluation). The note is framed as a request 'in addition to this license', not as a licence condition, so this is a confirmed OSI software licence with a non-binding usage request, not an NC/custom licence. GitHub's NOASSERTION is caused by the appended text defeating licensee's MIT match. access 'open-source' is correct under MAINTENANCE.md ('open-source requires a confirmed software licence'). Catalog convention checked: access_evidence appears only on the 11 source-available records and on none of the 262 open-source records, so none is added here. All other record claims re-checked today against primary sources and hold: category benchmark / autonomy B (benchmark harness, no agent of its own); domain; inputs (7 open-ended ML research-engineering environments, fixed time budgets); outputs (objective scores with starting/official-solution scores per task in README; human-expert comparison and agent trajectories per arXiv abstract); notes (MIT; password-protected solution zips). decisions.notes: Decision: correct. Main change: access open-source -> source-available with access_evidence (commercial_use false), following the September/August precedent for public unlicensed repos. Licence checked at root, every subdirectory (full recursive tree, 832 entries, not truncated), all 5 branches, README, and package metadata (none exists beyond requirements.txt): no licence of any kind. Second change: the notes' 'bundles Quantum ESPRESSO' / 'QE submodule' claim was already stale when the record was added (submodule removed 2025-12-18); the README still tells users to run git submodule update, which is out of date upstream. Kept unchanged: name, category, domain, autonomy A3-A4, inputs, outputs, paper/repo links. Autonomy was not re-assessed against the paper full text, so 'verified' stays 2026-06-16. Repo has branches named feat/assistant-hitl and fix/band-workflow-and-plan-hitl and a test_cluster_approval.py, which hint at human-approval gates for cluster submission; this is consistent with A3-A4 but was not examined further. The repo also contains src/vasp_agent.py (possible VASP support), not reflected in the record and not verified. The project website (tritondft.com) advertises a hosted live app; if the catalog wants to reflect that, a platform mention could be added in a later pass. All record URLs resolve (arXiv 200, GitHub 200). No lane-proposed problems existed for this record.
